Ariana placed first in her class for barrel racing and pole bending, while Svetalina placed third in barrel racing and second in pole bending.
Talk of the town
Locals warmly welcomed the rodeo's return.
Shire of East Pilbara president Anthony Middleton said Newman had been quietly buzzing in the lead-up to the event.
"There's a fair bit of talk; it hasn't happened since before COVID," he said.
"I didn't realise how important it was to the community … it's exciting to see."
Newman Campdraft and Rodeo Association president Cameron Wilson said it was special to bring rodeo back to Newman.
"It's going to be great for the town, great for the people, and just great to see it back in Newman," he said.
Mr Hall believed the turnout would be close to 1,300 people.
"I just think it's a great exercise for the town to show what we can produce; obviously, being such a small mining town, we don't have a lot of major events," he said.
"If we can establish this and keep it a recurring thing, I think it's only going to get bigger and better year on year."
Bringing rodeo back to the Pilbara
Launching Roebourne Rodeo last year, Karlayura Rodeo co-founder Tui Magner said it made sense for Karlayura to bring rodeo back to Newman.
"Myself, Brian Tucker and Georgina Bobby have really big dreams to activate rodeos more in the Pilbara," Ms Magner said.
"Doing Roebourne Rodeo in the west Pilbara, now coming over to the east has sort of been a perfect next step to build on that success.
"Newman itself has quite a long history in rodeo … we're just really trying to build on that success."
Competitors from as far north as the Kimberley region and as far away as the South West travelled for the full-points event.
Fellow Karlayura co-founder Georgina Bobby said Newman held a special place in the Karlayura team's heart.
"This place is in Nyiyiparli country, which is Brian Tucker's mother's homeland," she said.
"I think he wanted to bring it back here for his people."
Ms Bobby highlighted the relationship between Aboriginal stockmen and modern-day rodeo.
"Back in the day, the elders, old people then, they pretty much worked on stations," she said.
"It'll be good for them to see something that's come back with this rodeo, recognising those people."

title: Pan dulce y manufactura son Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la CDMX
content:
Aquí surgieron nuevas técnicas para piezas únicas
Conchas, chilindrinas, cuernos, gusanos, besos, orejas y puerquitos, parte de saberes y prácticas culinarias
Sábado 12 de septiembre de 2026, p. 26
El pan dulce mexicano, al igual que las prácticas y saberes para su elaboración, son Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Ciudad de México, al reconocerse sus valores culturales y sociales.
El decreto de la jefa de Gobierno, Clara Brugada, publicado ayer en la Gaceta Oficial, señala que si bien la forma de manufacturar el alimento fue introducida por los españoles, las necesidades y recursos propios de la panadería tradicional en la ciudad dieron lugar a nuevas técnicas y a un sistema cultural particular.
El decreto señala que la introducción del cultivo de trigo gestó una forma de elaborar el pan a partir de saberes particulares y generó, al mismo tiempo, un sistema gremial independiente, debidamente constituido y regulado, al trascender la actividad comercial en la que los panaderos comparten un sentido de identidad.
“Existen fuentes documentales que corroboran la presencia de panaderías y reposterías bien establecidas en la actual Ciudad de México desde el periodo de la Segunda Intervención Francesa.”
Enorme variedad para un sabor único
El texto que acompaña la resolución resalta que “el uso del pan en diversos actos sociales, tanto rituales como seculares, lo ha convertido en un elemento inherente a éstos, lo que ha dado lugar a la creación de piezas específicas para ciertas festividades”, y alude a un amplio abanico de piezas únicas por sus sabores, colores y texturas, que en panaderías llevan nombres como las tradicionales conchas de vainilla y chocolate, la chilindrina, gusano de canela, beso, chirimoya, cuerno, peineta, banderilla, puerquito, cocol, oreja, ojo de buey, mantecado, coyota o empanada rellena, entre otros.
“Se declara Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Ciudad de México a los saberes y prácticas del pan dulce tradicional” por constituir una manifestación de la memoria colectiva, las tradiciones, las costumbres y las celebraciones familiares y comunitarias, así como de los conocimientos transmitidos de generación en generación por la comunidad panadera”, señala el decreto que entra en vigor este 12 de septiembre.
La medida tiene la finalidad de salvaguardar los saberes y prácticas del pan dulce tradicional como símbolo cultural y social, mediante el reconocimiento, la dignificación, la promoción y la difusión de dichos valores.
De esa manera, dispone que la Secretaría de Cultura emita un plan de salvaguarda con el propósito de asegurar la identificación y divulgación de la expresión cultural protegida, incorporar la declaratoria a la Plataforma Digital del Patrimonio Cultural, Natural y Biocultural de la Ciudad de México.

title: Alberto de la Rosa, una vida de orgullo por la música jarocha
content:
El arpista es considerado uno de los mayores exponentes del instrumento en el mundo // Es fundador del grupo Tlen Huicani, que hoy cumple 53 años
Sábado 12 de septiembre de 2026, p. 3
“El movimiento arpista de Veracruz está vivo y con mucha fuerza”, afirma Alberto de la Rosa, compositor, arreglista y uno de los mayores exponentes del arpa jarocha en el mundo. Para el artista de 79 años, si antes ese instrumento estaba en Mandinga y Boca del Río, ahora Xalapa es uno de los principales centros de esta expresión, junto con Coatepec y Xico.
En el contexto del 53 aniversario del grupo Tlen Huicani, que se cumple hoy, De la Rosa afirma a La Jornada que la vigencia del arpa jarocha se explica por el apoyo de la Universidad Veracruzana (UV), los ayuntamientos locales, y sobre todo por el interés de la población en estudiar y ejecutar este instrumento.
Como muestra de su vitalidad, citó El Jarochódromo y el récord La Bamba, encuentros que reúnen a cientos de personas que bailan son jarocho en Coatepec y Xalapa, y que este año tendrán su octava y duodécima edición, respectivamente. También mencionó el Festival Internacional del Arpa Alberto de la Rosa, que en junio se realizó por cuarto año consecutivo, y convoca a músicos nacionales y extranjeros.
Entre los exponentes actuales, De la Rosa destaca a músicos jóvenes, como Horacio Martínez y Raúl Monge, quien canta, toca arpa y tiene en su haber más de 50 composiciones. Resalta la presencia de las mujeres, que en los años recientes se han interesado en la ejecución del instrumento.
Sobresale el caso de su hija María Cristina, quien en abril ganó el Premio del Público en el Concurso Mundial de Arpa 2026, que se celebra cada dos años en Holanda. “Logró ese reconocimiento por la emoción que despiertan sus interpretaciones y consiguió que los ojos del mundo artístico se fijen en México”.
De la Rosa se acercó a la música y aprendió a tocar la guitarra en Acayucan, en el sur de Veracruz, donde vivió hasta los 12 años. Recuerda que en un tiempo en que la radio y la televisión no eran frecuentes en los hogares veracruzanos, las familias se organizaban para realizar tertulias.
Los domingos, su mamá ponía una tarima y la música del arpista Andrés Huesca para bailar en su casa. “Era algo familiar; incluso, la palabra fandango ni siquiera se usaba, nada más decían: ‘va haber tarima’”, menciona.
“¿Yo por qué voy a tocar a Elvis?”
Entre los años 1950 y 1960, cuando el rock irrumpió con fuerza en México, De la Rosa quedó cautivado con Elvis Presley, y si bien lo siguió por un rato, llegó un momento en que se cuestionó sus gustos: “¿Yo por qué voy a tocar esa música, si soy veracruzano y mi música es el son jarocho?”.
A los 12 años, durante una semana del estudiante de la Escuela Preparatoria de Xalapa, presenció un concierto de arpa que desencadenó su interés por el instrumento. “Estaba escuchando al intérprete, cuando un amigo me contó que en su casa había un arpa, le pregunté quién la tocaba y me respondió que nadie. Así que le pedí que me la prestara y al otro día fui por ella”.
De la Rosa aprendió a tocar el arpa de forma autodidacta: escuchando discos y acercándose a quienes tocaban. “Los músicos de aquel tiempo eran celosos, quienes aprendían a tocar lo hacían de su papá o del tío. Yo me arrimaba a ellos y poco a poco hice amistad con algunos, hasta que Arcadio Solís me invitó a tocar con él”.
En las épocas de Carnaval o de Semana Santa, De la Rosa se unía a varios conjuntos. “Para que me dejaran andar con ellos no aceptaba nada de lo que ellos ganaban. Y como iba aprendiendo, y se corrió la voz de que no cobraba, otros grupos me empezaron a llamar”.
Después de un breve paso por la Escuela Nacional de Música, en la Ciudad de México, que se vio interrumpido por el movimiento estudiantil de 1968, De la Rosa regresó a Xalapa, adonde ingresó a la Normal Veracruzana Enrique C. Rébsamen, que tenía una intensa actividad artística. Era la época de Miguel Vélez en la danza, Mateo Oliva en la música y Antolín Guzmán, músico muy interesado en los jóvenes.
Como parte del Ballet Folklórico Veracruz, De la Rosa hizo una gira por Sudamérica, que se convirtió en una epifanía. “Me encontré con la sorpresa de que en todos los países había arpa; establecí relación con los intérpretes, traje un paquete de música e incluso un arpa de Venezuela, que es diferente a la nuestra”.
Después de aquellos recorridos, conformó el grupo Tlen Huicani, que dio su primer concierto oficial el 12 de septiembre de 1973, en el Teatro del Estado Ignacio de la Llave. Pronto, la UV se incorporó a la agrupación junto con la Orquesta Sinfónica de Xalapa y Orbis Tertius. “Más que pagar un sueldo, con la bandera de la universidad comenzamos a recibir invitaciones de muchas partes del mundo”.
Con casi 53 años de trayectoria, Tlen Huicani ha tenido presencia en 62 países. “Hemos dado la vuelta al mundo saliendo por el este y regresando por el oeste... infinidad de grabaciones, y Xalapa se ha convertido en la Ciudad del arpa”, subrayó.
Cuando se le pregunta qué enseñanza le ha dejado este instrumento, De la Rosa responde: el orgullo por la música veracruzana. “Ahora que hay una invasión de música de todo tipo, de alguna que podemos decir corriente, donde el éxito es la vulgaridad de los textos, tocar música jarocha es ir en contra de todo eso”.
En un mensaje para las nuevas generaciones, el arpista les pide “que echen un ojo y pongan el oído a la música folklórica. Muchos la consideran de segunda, pero no es así, a diferencia de otras expresiones que son pasajeras, ésta es nuestro orgullo y se mantiene en el tiempo”.
A las autoridades pide que abran más foros que permitan el intercambio de grupos como Tlen Huicani, con exponentes como Fernando de la Mora o la cantante Olivia Gorra, con quienes han alternado en otras ocasiones.
De cara al futuro, habló de la necesidad de documentar a los exponentes del arpa veracruzana y sus composiciones. “Hay gente que me ha preguntado: ‘¿cómo quisieras ser recordado?’ No, no me interesa ser recordado así. A mí me gustaría que sea recordado todo aquello por lo que he luchado, que sea recordado el son jarocho y que se fortalezca. Yo sólo fui y he sido uno de tantos que va pasando”, concluyó Alberto de la Rosa.

title: Roberto Rico Ramírez*: Las raíces del maoísmo en México
content:
propósito de la publicación del libro Estrella Roja en México y a 50 años de la muerte de Mao Zedong (9 de septiembre de 1976), Luis Hernández Navarro nos recuerda la presencia en México de la revolución China, dejando una huella profunda en nuestro país. La intelectualidad en esos tiempos, iniciando con Vicente Lombardo, pasando por Fernando Benítez y Lázaro Cárdenas, quedaron sorprendidos del gigante asiático.
El libro es un espejo de la trayectoria y práctica social de quien lo escribe; lo recuerdo por primera vez en aquella reunión que realizamos en Monterrey con la Coordinadora Línea de Masas. Siempre ha sido un luchador social, sus libros y sus artículos reflejan su orientación hacia el movimiento de masas, como Chiapas: La guerra y la Paz; No Habrá Recreo. Contra reforma constitucional y desobediencia magisterial y Siembra de Concreto Cosecha de Ira; Hermanos en Armas. La hora de los policías comunitarios y las autodefensas, seis libros con la Brigada para leer en libertad; En la serie Vientos del Pueblo, La primavera magisterial. Y en la colección popular, La pintura en la pared, ambos publicados por el Fondo de Cultura Económica, entre otros.
Luis desarrolla una disección quirúrgica de los grandes movimientos sociales y sus dispositivos militantes, de sus luchas desarrolladas al calor de las batallas sociales y su combinación con las luchas por los poderes locales. Luis Hernández, al mismo tiempo que detalla las acciones de los militantes, siembra el camino para mencionar las luchas que estos sujetos desarrollan. Tiene la habilidad y el punto fino para hacer investigaciones exhaustivas y entretejer la narrativa y, lo extraordinario, el uso de la narrativa para contar historia e historias de sus protagonistas, la narrativa es un arte que ágilmente desarrolla reconstruyendo al actor social, llevándonos a la reflexión y al desarrollo de pensamiento crítico del evento mismo.
Recuerdo al autor como luchador social cuando fue secretario general de la de la sección sindical de Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia y en la CNTE, éste también se la jugó muchas veces en marchas, paros y acciones que refleja en su talento como escritor. En esos tiempos había en el país un sinfín de grupos maoístas que se manejaban clandestinamente ante las fuerzas represoras del Estado. Algunos se jugaron la vida en la guerrilla, otros en el movimiento social, pero actuando con núcleos clandestinos, todos empujando los procesos de construcción del socialismo en México desde diferentes enfoques.
Ahí tenemos a dirigentes como Camilo Chávez, Edelmiro Maldonado, Esther Chapa, Vicente Estrada, Amador Tobon, Joel Aquino, José Santos, Judith Reyes, Antonio Martínez, Salvador Zarco, Paco Taibo II, entre otros, quienes apostaron por la construcción de potentes organizaciones de masas populares autónomas de base, de combativos contingentes estudiantiles y sindicales; algunos colocaban en el centro una columna de cuadros. Todos sujetos históricos que crearon su propia utopía que aún permea en la izquierda mexicana, con su diversidad, complementariedad y complejidad. Las únicas organizaciones de masas campesinas y populares que aún persisten en la izquierda mexicana son las creadas por los maoístas mexicanos. CNTE, MUP, CNPA; un sinnúmero de organizaciones barriales, comunitarias, ejidales, autónomas que aún siguen creando ideas comunitarias de decisión con sus paradigmas, extrayendo experiencias desde sus raíces culturales; ahí tenemos las formas de organización del EZLN, sembrando sus propios caminos en Chiapas como ejemplo, siempre en el centro de cualquier movimiento están los sujetos sociales que hacen posible la determinante cultural revolucionaria. El pueblo chino y Mao Zedong siempre han estado presentes en la izquierda mexicana. Como bien dice el autor: “no están todos los que son, pero sí algunos que permiten comprender momentos claves de nuestra historia reciente”. Esperemos su presentación en la FIL-Zócalo.
* Autor de El retorno. La Unión de Colonias Populares del Valle de México (UCP-VM): sus orígenes, sus organizaciones

title: Beyond mooncakes: rediscovering the harvest behind Mid-Autumn
content:
Traditionally, the festival marked a time to give thanks after months of labour in the fields, when communities could pause and celebrate abundance before the next cycle began.
That older idea has been given a distinctly Malaysian interpretation in a seasonal art installation in Kuala Lumpur’s Chinatown, where rice takes centre stage.
Visitors walking through the Kwai Chai Hong heritage alley will encounter rice sack-inspired lanterns, padi stalks, and harvest imagery intended to evoke the journey from field to table.
The choice of rice is deliberate. Beyond being a staple food, it carries memories, habits and lessons familiar across Malaysian households.
Co-organiser Zeen Chang said the installation was partly inspired by the reminders many children grow up hearing at the dining table: do not waste food, remember the effort behind it, and be grateful for what you have.
She pointed to the Chinese saying “li li jie xin ku”, which conveys the hard work behind every grain, and the Malay expression “kalau tak habis makan, nanti nasi menangis”.
Though different in language and origin, both encourage children to value food and recognise the labour behind it.
“Every grain of rice begins as a seed which, in turn, depends on fertile soil, favourable weather and countless hands before eventually reaching the table,” Chang told Bernama.
“That relationship between effort and abundance resonates across Malaysia’s cultures.”
The installation’s main pavilion draws inspiration from traditional rice mills and padi fields, using lanterns, rice sacks and rural motifs to bring that landscape into the city.
For visitors, the effect is less about faithfully recreating agricultural life than about making something ordinary feel visible again.
Chang said the story of rice is also one of interdependence. The rice eaten at one family’s table may have been planted, harvested, milled, transported and sold by people from entirely different communities.
That makes it an unexpectedly useful symbol for a festival often associated primarily with Chinese tradition.
Rice appears almost everywhere in Malaysian life – in homes, kopitiams, roadside stalls and restaurants, crossing ethnic and social boundaries with little fanfare.
“And perhaps it is precisely because it is so ordinary that its value can so easily be overlooked,” Chang said.
Another familiar object appears among the displays: the traditional rooster bowl, with its colourful bird motif and white ceramic body.
For many Malaysian Chinese families, the bowl is instantly recognisable from childhood kitchens, coffee shops and everyday meals, making it another object that connects memory with food.
The Mid-Autumn Festival falls on Sept 25 this year, and its contemporary celebrations may look very different from the farming communities that shaped its earliest traditions.
Yet the idea of harvest remains easy to understand, particularly in a country where food is such a central part of daily life.
It is a reminder that abundance rarely arrives on its own: behind a bowl of rice are weather, soil, labour, transport, and countless small acts and blessings that usually go unnoticed.

title: Inside the ancestral home of MCA founder Tan Cheng Lock
content:
But tucked amidst the bustle of the city is a place whose significance many may not know. It is the ancestral home of Tan Cheng Lock, the statesman and nation builder who founded MCA and became a leading voice for Malaya’s Chinese community.
A firm believer in a united, multiracial Malaya, Cheng Lock championed equal citizenship and cooperation among the country’s different communities, helping lay the foundations for the nation that would emerge.
Located on 111 Jalan Tan Cheng Lock, formerly Heeren Street, the house remains in the care of his descendants, who continue to preserve it as an important part of the family’s heritage.
According to Cheng Lock’s granddaughter, Tan Siok Choo, the house dates back to 1799 and was purchased by her great-great-grandfather, Tan Choon Bock, for use as the family home in 1875.
Cheng Lock lived there, while Siok Choo grew up in nearby Klebang Besar and visited about once a week. She did not enjoy these visits much as a child, as getting there meant a 45-minute journey along winding roads crowded with bullock carts.
“We also never really got to see my grandparents very much. I only gained more appreciation for the house later in life, when I was writing a book on it,” Siok Choo, 73, told FMT Lifestyle.
From the outside, the home resembles a traditional Melaka shophouse. Above its main gate hang two paper lanterns emblazoned with the Tan family name, which Siok Choo noted also carry a message about the importance of education.
“The lanterns say, ‘If you don’t educate your son, you have a donkey. If you don’t educate your daughter, you have a pig’,” she said.
“I was very impressed by how enlightened the person who created these lanterns was, especially in placing such importance on educating women, which was certainly not the norm at the time.”
The message appears very much in keeping with the late Cheng Lock’s progressive views on women’s equality.
One of the most striking things about the house is its sheer length, stretching across three courtyards. At the heart of the central courtyard stands a towering tree which, according to Siok Choo, was planted during her grandfather’s time and continues to flourish today.
According to Siok Choo, the house also played a part in the country’s political history, with Tunku Abdul Rahman holding meetings there with Chinese educationists to discuss the future direction of education in Malaya.
Her favourite part of the house is the first hall. Taking pride of place is an ornate altar dedicated to Guan Yu, beneath a sign bearing the Chinese characters for “Spirit of Righteousness”. Also displayed there are several statues of Guan Yu, as well as Kuan Yin, the goddess of mercy.
“In the altar, we have enshrined the family values of righteousness, loyalty and integrity, mercy and compassion,” Siok Choo said.
Its walls are also adorned with reproductions of essays written by the noted Song Dynasty poet Su Dongpo, known for building the famous “Pavilion of Timely Rain” in China.
The house’s second hall, known as the Hall of Filial Remembrance, contains another altar where Siok Choo conducts Confucian ancestor-remembrance rituals. She also offers fruit and Peranakan food at the altar.
“A lot of Chinese don’t have ancestral homes any more, so I think the ancestral remembrance ceremonies are slowly dying out. That’s quite a pity,” she said.
The rooms of the house are filled with photographs, documents and personal mementoes chronicling generations of the Tan family.
Hanging in the study where Cheng Lock once wrote his speeches, for example, is a rare photograph of Sultan Ibrahim Al-Masyhur of Johor with his last wife and daughter. The photograph is inscribed with Cheng Lock’s name and was personally sent to him.
The house’s upper floor contains the bridal chamber, as well as a bedroom where former prime minister Tunku Abdul Rahman would stay whenever he visited Cheng Lock.
Siok Choo also pointed out a four-poster bed which, according to Tunku Abdul Rahman’s memoirs, was rather uncomfortable to sleep in.
Tunku, however, was apparently too kind-hearted to ever tell her grandfather about it.
Maintaining the family home over the years has been a challenging and resource-intensive task. Siok Choo recalled that during the pandemic, the house went largely unattended for three years, resulting in the deterioration of many items within.
Despite these challenges, she remains deeply attached to her family’s ancestral home and hopes it will be preserved for future generations.
“It’s more than just a house; it really shaped my grandfather and the rest of my relatives by instilling in them values that influenced their views on life and family.
“I think that’s important, and I hope it will one day be passed down to my nephews and niece.”

title: Sir Gabriel Igbinedion, a tree who made several forests, by Dele Sobowale
content:
Dele Sobowale
“God could not be everywhere and, therefore, he made mothers” – Jewish proverb.
Sir (Chief) Gabriel Osawaru Igbinedion, the Esama of Benin Kingdom, born on Tuesday, September 11, 1934, like all of us, was created by the Almighty God; and moulded by his mother in a billion, Madam Okunozee Igbinedion. Together, God and Mama gifted to humanity one of the finest specimens of God’s creation one can know about.
The totality of Esama’s life and achievements leave those privileged to know about them in awe.
Though he prioritises God in his life, yet his testimonies about his wife deserves mention.
In a book titled, Chief GABRIEL OSAWARU IGBINEDION: THE CHRONICLES OF A LEGEND, written by Christopher Elomien, which was launched on Thursday, July 31, 2025 in Abuja, here is what our hero and worthy role model had to say about his mother:“Everything I am today, I owe to my mother. Mama was never idle, and she taught me the importance of diligence.
“She advised me, ‘My dear son, as you grow, do not covet another’s fortune’.
“She was fond of telling me, ‘My son, there are two histories in the world: the good and the bad: choose which one you want to belong to.’”
While that formed the foundation of a moral upbringing, the mother, who was a business woman, employing several people, dropped another gem on which Igbinedion fashioned his approach to managing businesses and non-profit organisations later in life.
“If you employ a fool, you will end up doing the work of a fool and your own.”
Cynics would say mother-love is common; and to some extent they are right.
However, very few eminently successful people, when asked, mention the influence of their mothers as a motivating factor.
They frequently list hard work, persistence, determination and financial prudence first.
Igbinedion is different in this regard. This is not the first book written on ‘the Esama of the World’, as the late Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Lamidi Adeyemi III, called him.
In several books published years earlier by Imam, H (2014), Great Igbinedion. Omoregie, O.S.B. (2008), Igbinedion of Africa. Orobator, S.E. (1995), Igbinedion: The Great Life of a Pioneer. Osaghae, E.E. (2017), Pioneering the Private University Sector in Nigeria: Legacies of Chief Gabriel Igbinedion, he had repeated the same tribute to his mother many times.
SERVING GOD AND MANKIND
“If I had served God as I served the King, he would not have forgotten me in my grey hairs”.
That was the lamentation of Cardinal Wolsey, 1475-1530, for several years the second most powerful man in Great Britain.
Wolsey, like Igbinedion, had risen from humble beginnings before being divinely propelled to the top.
He promptly decided to serve the crown instead of God and the people – until his downfall.
The Esama, right from the start, opted to serve God and humanity and did both splendidly.
His support for churches (several denominations) and mosques was unequalled.
Most other great Nigerian philanthropists invariably end up contesting for office; treating their donations as investments.
Igbinedion never contested for office. His relationship with God is explained in Chapter 10 of the book where the author informed us: “According to him, he hears revelations directly from God that have guided him in building numerous worship centres.
“Said Chief: ‘When God showed me in a dream to build Him two houses (two churches), I told God , ‘But, I have already built more than 40 churches’. He said ‘No! Build one in your compound and build one on Sapele Road’. So, I obeyed Him. “That is how the church in my compound and St Gabriel the Archangel Catholic Church Sapele Road came about. Since then, my life has been a blessing.”
His donations to churches and evangelism were monumental. According to the author: “He single-handedly built St Gabriel’s Catholic Church and donated it to the Archdiocese of Benin without seeking any form of recognition and appreciation from the Church.”
DEVOTED FAMILY MAN
“Many men can make a fortune but very few can build a family” – S Bryan.
A really happy family is one which ensures that no one is left behind. Igbinedion has achieved what is universally regarded as a mission impossible: to strive to build a great fortune and to keep a happy home at the same time.
The feat is made more remarkable by the fact that he had children with three different wives.
His father, who was a role model, died when he was still in primary school.
He was the only surviving child of his parents.
So, the transformation from bachelor to a loving patriarch of his own family was a personal effort and great achievement.
Central to this were four things: Good example, good education, good manners and good memories. Igbinedion paid great attention to details including neatness, punctuality and politeness exhibited by his children – male and female.
In Chapter 7 of the book, we discover that the busy businessman, who outsourced and delegated many things in life, paid personal attention to the discipline and upbringing of all his children.
The results are there to show in their lives.
TOP RANK NIGERIAN BUSINESS PIONEER
“All the [social and economic] growth takes place in the growing tip among the one percent of the population. It’s made up of pioneers, the beginners. That is where the action is” – Abraham Maslow, 1908-1970.
Igbinedion, quite rightly, is often associated with business.
But among those who knew him well, his pioneering spirit remains unequalled.
He was not among the one per cent opening new frontiers of business and education, he was the leading pioneer generating growth and opportunities where none existed.
Because of the trials (literally in a legal sense), tribulations and triumphs encountered by the trailblazers, it is not a role for the faint-hearted.
Courage, patience, perseverance and self-discipline are tested to the breaking point.
A few short sentences here cannot do justice to the entrepreneur who held the nation spell-bound for over forty years and is still a force to reckon with at 90+ and who gives the impression he could continue until 120 without diminished energy and creativity.
Chapters 5 and 6 provide a credible summary of the triumphs and disasters – while at the same time pointing to the booby traps which young and ambitious businessmen must avoid.
OKADA Airlines established in 1983 was symptomatic of his pioneering spirit.
It was the first private airline in Nigeria.
And, although the airline no longer operates, the impact was so astonishing that motor cycles adopted the name Okada, and today, Okada has entered the Oxford English dictionary – defined as “motorcycle taxis, a common mode of transportation in Nigeria and West African countries”.
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
“A tree does not make a forest”. That is conventional wisdom; not supported by facts of botany and biology.
Some trees, left alone and given sufficient land, can make forests.
In the human and social environment, anybody clinging to that false declaration has never met or heard about Chief Gabriel Igbinedion.
In over 45 years working in Nigeria, living and working in nine states, visiting all 36 states, at least forty times, I have not known of any other Nigerian who has single-handedly transformed a village – Okada – to a city in a generation; defined as 30 years as Chief Gabriel Igbinedion. Everything modern in Okada today was either established by him as a part of his long term development programme for his place of birth, or was built to take advantage of the opportunities which his visionary leadership induced.
Not surprisingly, the Igbinedion University and the Igbinedion Hospital and Medical Centre receive most of the attention.
They epitomise his decision to give the best possible education and healthcare to his people in particular and fellow Nigerians in general.
Because a university and teaching hospital cannot operate without support, he has had to provide power and water to the institutions, hostels and a great part of the surrounding community.
A man whose formal education ended in secondary school is now an employer of professors in every field of learning.
CONCLUSION
“A well-written life is as rare as a well-spent one” – Thomas Carlyle, 1795-1881.
Elomien’s book on Igbinedion is not the first one that I have read.
But, it is certainly the best researched and factually presented.
It was a valiant effort – worthy of a life gloriously spent.
There is more to learn about this extra-ordinary man than space would allow now.
But, serialisation of the book starts tomorrow morning.
•Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola.
This article was first published in 2025

title: No POP or Paper Mâché: This Family Celebrates Ganesh Chaturthi With Wheat, Mud & a Growing Idol
content: On the first day, it looks almost too simple to be Ganpati. A large plate. A thin layer of finely sifted mud. And, carefully marked on its surface, the familiar outline of Ganesha — his trunk, ears, rounded belly and little crown. Then come the seeds. One by one, wheat kernels are placed along the outline, with just enough space between them to allow each seed to grow. Water is sprinkled over the mud. The family recites the Gayatri Mantra 12 times. Then they wait, and by the second day, tiny green shoots begin to appear. Over the next few days, they grow taller, slowly filling the outline. By the fifth day, the little kernels have transformed into lush green blades, tracing the unmistakable form of Ganesha. At a certain height and angle, the effect is almost magical: Bappa has appeared, not through clay or plaster, but through something living. For Pratiksha Marathe and her parents in Kalyan, Maharashtra, this is their Vanaspati Ganesh — a tradition that has become one of the most meaningful parts of their Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations. The family uses mud, wheat seeds, sunlight and water to create their Ganpati, without plaster, paint or thermocol. “It feels like therapy to create your own version of Ganesha,” says Pratiksha. This year marks the family’s 31st year of celebrating the festival at home. What began in 1995 with a conventional idol has slowly evolved into a celebration that asks a very different question: what if bringing Ganesha home did not have to mean leaving an idol behind in nature? A festival that began with an idol For years, Ganesh Chaturthi in the Marathe household followed a familiar rhythm. Pratiksha, her parents, relatives, neighbours, and close family friends would welcome Ganpati home. There would be puja, aarti, homemade modaks and laddoos, followed by visarjan on the second day. But Pratiksha remembers another part of the festival just as vividly: the scenes that followed. Seeing “thousands of idols lying after the visarjan on Dadar Chowpatty and many other visarjan places” made her think about what happened after the celebrations ended. “What means the world to us is somewhere not accepted by nature. Maybe it’s time to celebrate festivals differently,” she recalls thinking. For the Marathe family in Kalyan, their Vanaspati Ganesh has become a 31-year-old festival tradition with a different approach to visarjan. The family first moved away from plaster of Paris idols and tried Shadu clay, or natural river clay. But even that raised questions about how completely the material returned to nature. Then came 2020. During the pandemic, when getting an idol was difficult, the family still wanted to preserve their decades-old tradition. That was when they turned to an idea they had encountered through their long association with Manashakti Research Centre in Lonavala. The concept was Vanaspati Ganesh — using growing wheat seedlings to create the form of Ganesha. Soon, it became their own annual ritual. It starts with mud, seeds, and a little patience Three or four days before Ganesh Chaturthi, Pratiksha’s father begins preparing the base. He collects mud from the surrounding area, filters and sifts it, then mixes it with water and spreads roughly an inch-thick layer into a large, 18-inch plate. Once the base is ready, Pratiksha draws a simple outline of Ganesha. Her mother sets aside good-quality wheat seeds, which are carefully placed along the outline with enough space for the shoots to grow. Water is sprinkled over the plate as the family recites the Gayatri Mantra 12 times. For the family, all their prayers, aartis, mantras are intentional which creates a calm, positive atmosphere for the seeds to grow. Pratiksha carefully places wheat kernels along the hand-drawn outline of Ganesha, leaving enough space for the shoots to grow. Then the plate is placed where the plants can receive sunlight and is watered twice a day. No plaster, paint or thermocol. Just mud, seeds, sunlight and care. And then, Bappa begins to grow The transformation is what makes the ritual particularly fascinating for children. On Day 1, the wheat kernels are still clearly visible. “By the next day, tiny sprouts begin pushing through the mud. Soon, they turn green and begin growing like blades of grass,” says Pratiksha. Slowly, the green shoots fill the entire outline. By the fifth day, the wheatgrass can grow to around a foot in length. From a particular height and angle, the outline of Ganesha becomes strikingly clear. Children from the neighbourhood often stop to look. Some even imagine what it would be like to make a gigantic version outdoors — a Ganpati visible from the sky. For Pratiksha, however, its meaning goes beyond the novelty. A celebration where nothing is left behind The family’s two-day celebration still retains everything that makes Ganesh Chaturthi special. Their fibre-based Ganesha idol is used for puja every year and is never immersed. There are aartis in the morning and evening, homemade modaks, laddoos, fruits, prayers, and the chanting of Ganesha’s name. On the second day, instead of immersing an idol, they perform a symbolic visarjan by immersing a supari in water. Instead of immersing an idol, the family performs a symbolic visarjan with a supari, while the wheatgrass is harvested and shared as prasad. The wheatgrass completes its own cycle. It is harvested and eaten as prasad, with some also added to everyday food. The mud is either reused the following year or mixed into their house plants. When friends and neighbours learnt about the tradition, some even began asking the family to keep aside wheatgrass for them as prasad. Even the decorations have changed The family’s sustainability journey does not end with the Ganpati. Pratiksha’s father has traditionally been in charge of the decorations, and she began helping him as she grew older. One material they consciously moved away from was thermocol. “When I was in school, I learnt that thermocol is difficult to recycle and can become a persistent pollutant. Since then, we have increasingly relied on cardboard flowers and paper-based decorations instead,” she says. It is a small change, but one that reflects their larger philosophy: festive does not have to mean wasteful. What Bappa leaves behind For Pratiksha, perhaps the most beautiful part of the Vanaspati Ganesh is what happens at the end. The wheat that arrives as tiny seeds eventually becomes something the family can eat. In that sense, Ganesha does not simply disappear after visarjan. He becomes part of the family in another form — returning to the body through food and, eventually, to the earth. From cardboard flowers to paper decorations, the Marathe family has gradually found ways to make their Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations less wasteful. The idea also connects with what Ganesha represents to the family. Pratiksha describes him as the God of intelligence, the remover of obstacles and someone whose stories offer lessons about gratitude, empathy and problem-solving. In an age of increasing dependence on AI, she believes the festival can also be a reminder to retain our ability to think, assess situations and solve problems. “Can we be more empathetic and grateful towards each other?” she asks. Keeping the celebration, changing the way we celebrate Ganesh Chaturthi is much bigger than an idol. It is the neighbours dropping by, the aarti everyone gathers for, steaming modaks, children watching decorations come together and, in Mumbai, the unmistakable energy that takes over entire neighbourhoods. The Marathe family does not want to take away any of that. They simply believe the celebration can evolve. Families can make clay idols at workshops, opt for artificial ponds for visarjan, choose reusable decorations or even volunteer for beach clean-ups after the festivities. The wheatgrass that forms their Vanaspati Ganesh is eventually harvested and eaten as prasad, completing its journey from seed to food. “Festivals are important,” says Pratiksha. “They give a sense of purpose as a community.” But perhaps the responsibility that comes with that joy is just as important. The question is not whether we should celebrate. It is how we can celebrate in a way that allows both our traditions and the environment to breathe. And perhaps that is what makes this little green Ganpati so powerful. He arrives as a handful of seeds, grows through days of prayer and care, becomes prasad, and finally returns to the earth. Nothing is really lost. The celebration simply changes form. All images courtesy Pratiksha Marathe

title: Netball team's emotion-filled win after player killed in car crash
content:
Netball team's emotion-filled win after player killed in car crash
In short:
An A-grade netball team in Victoria's Wimmera region has won a high-emotion grand final after one of its most talented young players died in a car crash this week.
The Navarre Grasshoppers beat the Carisbrook Redbacks 58-51 in the Maryborough Castlemaine District Netball League decider.
What's next?
The team has been celebrated for its bravery, skill and determination, to win the game in honour of teammate Zanaiya Bergen.
The Navarre Grasshoppers have triumphed in a scenario no sporting team should ever have to face.
One of their most talented young players, 23-year-old Zanaiya Bergen, died on Thursday evening when her car hit a tree after training.
She and her teammates were on the verge of making history, after snapping Avoca's 69-game winning streak in a thrilling Maryborough Castlemaine District Netball League (MCDNL) preliminary final just days earlier.
In what was Zanaiya's debut season in the MCDNL, the goal shooter was one of five Navarre players named in the team of the year.
Her unexpected death cast doubt on whether her team would even play on Saturday.
Do it for Zee
Zanaiya, or Zee as she was affectionately known, had played 18 games for her new club, scoring 664 goals across the 2026 season.
She had previously featured in A-grade matches for Stawell in the Wimmera Football Netball League, and Rupanyup in the Horsham District Football Netball League.
MCDNL netball coordinator Katrina Turner said the league had spent most of Friday speaking with the Navarre Football Netball Club about whether the finals would go ahead.
"Whatever they decided, we would fully support them with what they wanted to do," Ms Turner said.
"When they called and said they wanted to play, I called their opponents in the A-grade and C-grade to let them know."
Zanaiya's name remained on the scoresheet for Saturday's grand final, and a minute's silence was held at the start of the game.
Purple ribbons and black arm bands were worn to mark the tragedy.
As the day went on, a significant crowd surrounded the Princes Park netball court at Maryborough to witness an A-grade match which was tense, competitive, and above all, highly emotive.
Zanaiya's teammates were doing all they could to win in honour of their teammate.
Emotion overcame some players as the game neared its end, and despite the heartbreaking circumstances, as the final whistle was blown the Navarre Grasshoppers came away with the win, 58-51.
Video of the match showed some players overwhelmed with tears the moment the game finished.
Members of the Navarre Football Netball Club have been offered counselling.
A premiership medal will go to Zanaiya's family.
Tributes far and wide
Zanaiya has been remembered as a funny, energetic, loyal and kind person.
Outside of her netball accolades, she spent five and a half years as a personal aged care worker at Eventide Homes in Stawell.
Her employer posted a social media tribute, which said Zanaiya brought warmth, laughter, kindness and genuine connection to every interaction.
"Zee leaves behind an enormous hole in our workplace and, most importantly, in the hearts of the residents and people she cared for so deeply," the post read.
"We will miss her more than words can express and will forever be grateful that she was part of our Eventide family."

title: Così le donne indigene del Brasile proteggono la loro foreste conservando semi e praticando agroecologia. In arrivo una mappa mondiale per promuoverle
content:
Così le donne indigene del Brasile proteggono la loro foreste conservando semi e praticando agroecologia. In arrivo una mappa mondiale per promuoverle
Indice
Nel Pará, in Brasile, le donne hanno un ruolo centrale nell’agricoltura e nella difesa dei territori. Nel distretto di Nawalparasi, in Nepal, gruppi di abitanti gestiscono direttamente le loro foreste comunitarie. Altrove si conservano semi, si pratica agroecologia, si difendono terre minacciate dall’estrazione di risorse. Esperienze lontane migliaia di chilometri che presto dovrebbero finire nello stesso posto: una mappa mondiale delle soluzioni locali per foreste, clima e biodiversità.
La Global Forest Coalition, una coalizione internazionale di ONG e organizzazioni dei Popoli indigeni che lavora sui diritti delle comunità legate alle foreste, ha annunciato il progetto Gender-Just Real Solutions Map for Forests and Communities: il lancio è previsto per novembre 2026. Per ora si stanno costruendo criteri, metodologia e prime schede insieme alle organizzazioni che lavorano nei territori.
Alla costruzione della mappa partecipano gruppi di Bangladesh, Brasile, Colombia, Cile, Repubblica Democratica del Congo, Honduras, Nepal, Panama e Zambia, insieme a reti regionali e internazionali. Il lavoro viene portato avanti con il Critical Geography Collective e con il sostegno di Bread for the World e Rosa Luxemburg Foundation.
Non sarà una collezione di puntini verdi
L’idea è evitare la classica mappa dove si clicca su una bandierina, compare il nome di un progetto e finisce lì. Ogni voce dovrebbe raccontare cosa sta facendo una comunità, chi partecipa, dove, da quanto tempo e quali condizioni hanno permesso a quell’esperienza di esistere. Dentro potranno entrare pratiche di agroecologia, protezione delle foreste, saperi tradizionali, forme di sostentamento locale e territori difesi dalle attività estrattive.
Durante tre incontri online svolti tra luglio e agosto, le organizzazioni coinvolte hanno stabilito un principio abbastanza netto: le iniziative dovranno essere concrete e radicate in un territorio. Niente ricette confezionate da replicare identiche da un continente all’altro. Il terreno, le persone, i rapporti di potere e perfino gli ostacoli cambiano. La soluzione universale pronta per l’esportazione può quindi accomodarsi fuori dalla porta.
C’è però una cautela che evita di trasformare il progetto in qualcosa che ancora non è. La definizione di Real Solutions, “soluzioni reali”, appartiene alla cornice adottata dalla stessa Global Forest Coalition. I criteri di inclusione ed esclusione sono ancora in fase di validazione e le prime voci della mappa non sono state pubblicate. Non siamo quindi davanti a una classifica scientifica delle politiche climatiche più efficaci, bensì a uno strumento costruito per documentare e condividere pratiche che la rete identifica come comunitarie, territoriali e rispettose dei diritti.
“Gender-just” significa anche chiedere chi decide
La parte forse più interessante arriva prima ancora di parlare di alberi. Per stabilire se un’esperienza possa essere considerata davvero equa dal punto di vista di genere, il gruppo non vuole limitarsi a contare quante donne partecipano a una riunione. Vuole guardare chi svolge il lavoro, compreso quello domestico e di cura, chi prende le decisioni, chi controlla la terra, le risorse e il reddito.
Jaqueline Santos, della brasiliana FASE, ha portato l’esempio del Pará, dove le donne hanno un ruolo importante nell’agricoltura e nella protezione dei territori, ma nelle zone rurali possono incontrare enormi difficoltà nell’accedere ai sistemi formali di sostegno quando subiscono violenza. Da anni la stessa FASE lavora con gruppi di produttrici e realtà agroecologiche nello Stato brasiliano, legando autonomia economica e organizzazione delle donne.
Dal Kivu, nella Repubblica Democratica del Congo, Ariella Kabunga del PIDP ha posto un altro limite molto concreto: avere leggi formalmente attente alla parità serve poco se le donne vengono invitate ai tavoli senza poter incidere sulle decisioni. La partecipazione, nella logica con cui si sta costruendo la mappa, deve comprendere anche potere effettivo, responsabilità e possibilità di orientare le scelte della comunità.
Anche in Nepal questo rapporto tra foreste e autonomia passa direttamente attraverso l’organizzazione locale. La Federation of Community Forestry Users Nepal, una delle realtà coinvolte nel progetto, lavora da decenni con gruppi di utenti delle foreste comunitarie. In alcune esperienze le donne gestiscono direttamente attività agroforestali, partecipano alle decisioni e organizzano produzione e raccolta. In una foresta comunitaria del distretto di Makawanpur, per esempio, un gruppo composto da quaranta donne ha avviato la coltivazione della curcuma su un’area precedentemente inutilizzata.
Sulla mappa finiranno anche le cose che fanno fallire le soluzioni
Raccontare soltanto le esperienze riuscite avrebbe prodotto una bella vetrina. Il progetto vuole invece registrare anche ciò che le rende fragili o impedisce loro di crescere. Durante la costruzione della metodologia sono emersi progetti estrattivi, accaparramento delle terre, norme patriarcali, apparati legislativi ereditati dal colonialismo, burocrazia, scarsità di finanziamenti e criminalizzazione di chi difende l’ambiente.
È un’impostazione che la Global Forest Coalition porta avanti da tempo. Nel rapporto From False Solutions to Transformative Change, pubblicato a gennaio 2026, la rete aveva raccolto casi da Bangladesh, Bolivia, Cile, Marocco, Panama e Zambia proprio per mostrare insieme le iniziative comunitarie e le condizioni economiche e politiche che possono ostacolarle.
La nuova mappa prova a trasformare quel lavoro in uno strumento consultabile e destinato a crescere. Le organizzazioni e i gruppi comunitari possono già proporre iniziative da valutare per l’inserimento e, dopo il lancio di novembre, il database dovrebbe continuare ad aggiornarsi.
Quando sarà online, quindi, sulla schermata dovrebbero comparire foreste, campi, comunità, gruppi di donne e territori molto diversi tra loro. Dietro ogni punto, però, ci sarà anche tutto quello che normalmente scompare dalle mappe: chi possiede la terra, chi lavora, chi decide, chi riesce a restare e chi deve difendersi per continuare a farlo. Forse è proprio per questo che, prima di tracciare i confini, hanno cominciato dalle persone.
Ti potrebbe interessare anche:
- In Perù hanno rimesso in funzione i waru waru inca: 3.000 anni dopo aiutano ancora le patate contro il clima estremo
- Nei villaggi della Tanzania la crisi climatica si combatte con alveari, pollai e donne finalmente ammesse alle decisioni
- In Etiopia una cooperativa bruciava 2.305 litri di diesel in tre mesi: ora irriga i campi grazie all’energia solare
- A Nairobi sono le donne a tenere in piedi “le baracche” e i quartieri durante le alluvioni o il caldo estremo
- Mentre i villaggi si prosciugano e il deserto avanza, le donne in Marocco scalano le montagne per catturare la nebbia e trasformarla in acqua potabile

title: Tradisjonsrikt utvær legg ned: – Ei varsla krise for ærfuglen
content:
Selskapet melder sjølv om nedlegginga på Facebook, og oppgir nedgangen i ærfuglbestanden som hovudårsak.
Det markerer slutten på ein æra for ein av dei mest unike tradisjonane langs kysten vår.
I generasjonar har øyfolka på Helgeland levd i eit tett og livsviktig samspel med ærfuglen, populært kalla «ea».
Menneska har bygd reir og verna fuglane mot rovdyr i hekketida, og som takk har dei kunna sanke dei verdifulle edderduna når fuglane forlét reira utpå sommaren.
No er derimot fuglebestanden i så stor nedgang at drifta til selskapet ikkje lenger er berekraftig.
Luksusdyner til dei kongelege
– Dei siste åra har talet på ærfuglar som kjem til Lånan gått mykje ned. I år hadde vi berre halvparten så mange fuglar som i 2018, seier fuglevaktar Hildegunn Nordum.
Konsekvensen av at det blir færre fuglar på reir, er at det blir mindre edderdun og dermed færre dyner å produsere og selje.
Edderdun frå ærfugl blir rekna for å vere verdas varmaste og mest eksklusive duner. Det krevst dun frå omtrent 60 reir for å lage éi dyne av vanleg størrelse, og ei slik handlaga dyne har hatt ein prislapp på godt over 100.000 kroner.
Dynene blir rekna som ei investering som kan vare i fleire generasjonar. Blant dei som søv under desse dynene dronning Sonja. I 2007 gjekk kommunane på Helgeland saman om å gi slike dyner i 70-årsgåve til kongeparet.
Arbeidet med å reinse duna går føre seg tradisjonelt for hand på ein såkalla dunharpe for å skilje ut støv og rask, og er eit tidkrevjande arbeid.
– Det er nesten eit halvt års arbeid for å få ferdig duna til éi dyne, forklarer Nordum.
Tradisjonen med å la fuglevaktarar bygge små hus og reir til ærfuglane, for så å sanke duna når fuglane forlèt reiret, strekker seg heile 1500 år tilbake i tid.
Dette unike samspelet mellom fugl og menneske bidrog sterkt til at Vegaøyane i 2004 hamna på UNESCOs liste over natur- og kulturarven i verda.
Varsla katastrofe: – Det ser f* meg mørkt ut
Nedlegginga av Utværet Lånan AS speglar ei dramatisk utvikling som lenge har prega Helgelandskysten.
Forsking bekreftar at ærfuglbestanden i verdsarvområdet er meir enn halvert berre dei siste ti åra.
På Hysvær har fuglevaktarane Snefrid Jakobsen og Øystein Ludvigsen nyleg slått alarm om situasjonen.
– Vi reknar med cirka 80 prosent tilbakegang, kanskje meir, sidan 90-talet, seier Jakobsen om utviklinga.
Ludvigsen har uttrykt frykt for at ærfuglen på Vega kan vere heilt borte om 10–15 år viss trenden fortset.
– Det ser f*** meg mørkt ut.
Årsakene til tilbakegangen er ifølge forskinga samansette, og kjem av ein kombinasjon av klimaendringar med varmare hav, dårlegare næringsinnhald i maten deira, menneskelege forstyrringar frå båttrafikk, og dessutan auka press frå rovdyr som oter, mink, havørn og kråke.
– Kvar einaste fugl vi klarer å berge og hjelpe trygt ut i havet, er ein siger, seier Jakobsen.
– Det skjer stort sett overalt der ein har noko data. Einaste unntak, ironisk nok, ser ut til å vere indre Oslofjord. Der har det vore ein auke over dei siste åra
Det seier sjøfuglforskar Jan Bustenes i Norsk institutt for naturforsking (Nina) som nettopp har vore i felt på Vega med prosjektet «Allianse for ærfugl».
Bustenes er einige med vaktarane i at det blir ekstremt vanskeleg å få bestanden tilbake til historiske høgder.
– Spørsmålet nå er om ein i det heile klarer å berge bestanden og stabilisere han på eit nivå der han klarer å halde oppe seg sjølv, seier han.
Transportproblem gav nådestøyten
På Lånan har dei merka desse miljøendringane på nært hald gjennom dei 20 åra selskapet har eksistert.
– Det er lite mat til fuglane. Vêret har også forandra seg. Eg håpar verkeleg praten om dette kan bidra til at det blir meir forsking på kva som skjer, for det er kjempeviktig, understrekar Nordum.
Men for Lånan AS var ikkje mangelen på fugl det einaste problemet.
Den andre medverkande årsaka til avviklinga er at båtturane mellom Vega og Lånan fall bort.
Selskapet prøvde ein periode å organisere eigne turar til Lånan etter at dei faste båtturane, som i dei første åra hadde tre anløp i veka, stansa.
– Nå må vi erkjenne at vi ikkje har moglegheit for å drive dette vidare. Det lønner seg ikkje, seier Nordum.
Dette skjer sjølv om selskapet tidlegare har fått økonomiske tilskot frå blant anna Innovasjon Noreg, Nordland fylkeskommune og Riksantikvarens verdiskapingsprogram.
Sjølv om selskapet nå set punktum, vil ikkje ærfuglane på Lånan bli overlatne til seg sjølve.
– Vi skal fortsette å vere fuglevaktarar. Ea og ærfuglen er det viktigaste for oss, så den kulturarven fortset vi å ta vare på, seier Nordum.
– Men formidlingsbiten blir borte. Vi er jo det ekte, vi er jo kulturarven. Det blir borte for folk å oppleve og sjå.
Så lenge det er ærfugl og dun på øya, vil fuglevaktarane fortsette å lage så mange dyner dei kan.

title: ‘Bir Ganeshman’: A theatrical tribute to a freedom fighter
content:
Columns
‘Bir Ganeshman’: A theatrical tribute to a freedom fighter
At a moment when history is on the cusp of major transformation, creating a play based on the life and work of a dedicated politician and freedom fighter feels like deeply meaningful ‘karma’.Abhi Subedi
I was struck by an invitation from Ashesh Malla, the director, creator and pioneer of the Sarwanam theatre group, to see the play—Bir Ganeshman— on August 30, 2026, at Sarwanam Theatre in Kathmandu. The play, which he wrote and directed, is about the widely respected politician and freedom fighter Ganesh Man Singh (1925-97). I woke from the shock and confusion of the Bhotekoshi deluge of August 26, 2026, as it were. Sarwanam, Malla declared, also held donation programmes for the flood victims.
I was drawn to the play for several other reasons as well. First, I have been associated with this theatre since its inception 45 years ago and have written reviews and the history of this group a number of times. The continuum of this theatre group has become a phenomenon. Several theatre groups were formed at different times, including the famous Arohan Theatre, but they could not maintain their continuity. Several other theatres, run mainly by artists and dedicated people of the younger generation, are active today; this is inspiring and encouraging.
Staging the lives of Bir ‘brave’ or noted persons has been a familiar subject in theatrical tradition. This theme inspired dramatists from Shakespeare of Britain to Balakrishna Sama of Nepal. As someone who teaches this topic in the Department of English at Tribhuvan University, I can allude to the plays of English dramatists. Shakespeare comes first in dramatising the lives of powerful rulers and leaders.
A dramatist’s choice of persona for theatre often involves politicians and people in power playing roles that address matters affecting politics. The German playwright and politically oriented thinker Bertolt Brecht wrote plays that critics call politically oriented. His play The Resistible Rise of Arturo Ui (1941), which evokes prophetic matters like the story of the rise of Hitler, has become a subject of critical interpretation among those who find this theme meaningful and relevant at all times. Playwrights have written on the lives of politicians and their struggle to achieve political goals. The focus in all cases is on the goal materialised by the politician for the amelioration of the people. In such plays, the theatrical performances of the protagonist are projected on different planes.
The protagonist’s private life, his/her agony and moments of satisfaction constitute the main components of such plays. For the dramatist, the struggle of the character, who is a politician or a leader of a certain movement, to perennially adjust his or her public and private life forms the basis of the play.
We have examples of several foundational leaders of Asia, known as revolutionary architects of the movements being projected, as protagonists. In some cases, the official propaganda machinery valorises leaders in power as heroes and liberators. Their memories and narratives of struggle form the principal theme, which would also be the moral basis of the play. They could be famous politicians or leaders who have made an impact on history. The advantage of casting them as protagonists is that they can be staged, or their stories can become the principal motif of the performance for the audience.
Such plays bring one other question to the fore: is a playwright taking the side of the politician, or is he writing with ambivalence? Theatre scholars, critics, and members of the public always ask this question. Brecht, in The Resistible Rise of Arturo Ui, is not on the side of the protagonist Hitler. Similarly, the famous American playwright Arthur Miller wrote The Crucible (1953), which dramatises the Salem witch trials of 1692 to debunk Senator Joe McCarthy’s political prosecution plans known famously as McCarthyism. Miller’s resonance can be felt in a number of other political plays. One example is One for the Road (1984) by British playwright Harold Pinter.
Playwright Ashesh Malla’s play on Singh is based on his memoirs and historical records. Malla’s play Bir Ganeshman represents the call of history that many people responded to by waking up and acting. This includes not only people associated with Singh’s party, the Nepali Congress, but also other political groups, including communist parties. Singh wanted to keep the ideal of democracy and people’s rights as the principal dharma that demanded honesty and sacrifice from the people. Singh’s expressions about the famous notion of people, their pursuits, and even their perceptions of him are revealing.
Summing up Ganesh Man Singh, I have previously written in this paper: “Some episodic and liminal moments of Singh's life are commonly mentioned. They are: Singh broke Bhadragol jail before 1950 and escaped to India where he joined BP Koirala, spent eight years in the Sundarijal detention camp from 1960, led the mass movement of 1990, and declined the offer made by king Birendra to become prime minister after the fall of the Panchayat system in 1990. These events highlight Singh's revolutionary character and his democratic ideals.”
Malla explores conflict, tension, quest and irresolution in this play, which took him a long time to write and Sabitri Malla to edit. The dominant mood of the oeuvre is that of respect. The persona of Ganesh Man Singh is presented as a hero undaunted and above any worldly gains. The characters, including the protagonist, the chorus and others, have brilliantly played their roles.
Malla and Sarwanam Theatre Group want to use this play, Bir Ganeshman, to awaken the young generation to important moments in history and familiarise them with historical actors and their roles. Essentially, it is to show how the courage of a leader like Singh can bring democratic transformation. We should appreciate this messianic zeal of the senior playwright Ashesh Malla, who has maintained this spirit for nearly half a century. At a moment when history is on the cusp of important transformation, creating a natak (play) based on the life and work of a dedicated politician and freedom fighter is a deeply meaningful karma.

title: Karakachoff: el radical que quiso cambiar la política
content:
Matilde Karakachoff tenía cuatro años cuando mataron a su padre. Durante mucho tiempo, Sergio fue para ella una figura reconstruida a partir de los relatos de otros. Estaban las historias de su madre, las conversaciones de su abuela, los recuerdos de los compañeros de militancia y las visitas de amigos que ayudaron a mantener presente la imagen del hombre que había sido asesinado en La Plata.
Uno de esos recuerdos familiares apareció después de las elecciones de 1983. Raúl Alfonsín había ganado la Presidencia y la madre de Matilde lloraba. La niña todavía no comprendía lo que significaba aquella elección ni la trayectoria política de su padre. Su madre sí. “Si tu papá estuviera vivo, por ahí estaría en el lugar de Alfonsín”, le dijo.
Tal vez presidente, tal vez en ese lugar de conducción que la recuperación democrática acababa de poner en manos de una generación de radicales. Para Matilde, aquella frase fue una de las primeras señales de que Sergio Karakachoff había sido algo más que su padre. Hasta entonces conocía su ausencia y había aprendido a convivir con las consecuencias de esa muerte. Después empezó a comprender su dimensión pública, el lugar que había ocupado dentro de una generación política y la historia que había quedado interrumpida aquel 10 de septiembre de 1976.
Mucho antes de convertirse en una víctima de la dictadura, Karakachoff había sido un adolescente que se acercó al radicalismo casi por curiosidad. Su madre contaba que, cuando tenía alrededor de 14 años, había entrado a un comité de la Unión Cívica Radical porque era el único lugar que veía iluminado de noche. Había gente reunida, se escuchaban conversaciones y quiso saber qué ocurría allí. Esa curiosidad terminó convirtiéndose en militancia.
Matilde vinculó esa historia con una característica que, según quienes lo conocieron, atravesó toda su vida política. “Fue un militante que leía, que escribía, que estudiaba”, dijo. Su madre repetía que podía pasar horas trabajando, conversando y discutiendo. “Se pasaba horas y horas escribiendo, y obviamente conversando también, y discutiendo, y realmente dándole palabra a la política”. Para su hija, era “realmente un pensador, una persona que sobre todo pensaba, que escribía y que elaboraba el pensamiento de la política desde el punto de vista del radicalismo y la militancia”.
Esa dimensión aparece también en los recuerdos de Federico “Freddy” Storani, uno de los dirigentes que compartió con él aquella experiencia política desde la juventud. Lo recuerda como un dirigente “muy bien formado intelectualmente”, pero también como alguien cuya forma de discutir podía ser incómoda: “Tenía una lengua filosa, era ácido, sarcástico e irónico en los debates”. Con los más jóvenes, sin embargo, tenía otra actitud. “Era muy contenedor con nosotros que éramos más jóvenes”, recuerda.
La combinación ayuda a explicar el lugar que ocupó dentro de la política platense de aquellos años. Podía discutir con dureza y, al mismo tiempo, convertirse en una referencia para una generación que todavía estaba aprendiendo a hacer política.
Del Colegio Nacional a la Coordinadora. Sergio Karakachoff nació en La Plata el 27 de junio de 1939. Fue en el Colegio Nacional Rafael Hernández donde adquirió una de sus primeras dimensiones públicas. Allí fundó el Centro de Estudiantes Democráticos y comenzó una actividad que después atravesaría toda su vida: combinar organización, discusión política y construcción colectiva.
En la Universidad Nacional de La Plata estudió Derecho y participó activamente del movimiento estudiantil. Fue uno de los protagonistas de la conformación de Franja Morada, el espacio universitario que comenzó a tomar forma nacional a fines de los años 60 y que estaba vinculado con la tradición de la Reforma Universitaria de 1918. En sus primeros tiempos reunía a jóvenes de distintas tradiciones políticas, aunque el radicalismo fue adquiriendo una presencia cada vez más determinante.
Karakachoff se recibió de abogado en 1965. Antes había sido secretario legislativo del Concejo Deliberante de La Plata, entre 1963 y 1964. Su profesión se convirtió en otra herramienta de intervención en una sociedad atravesada por conflictos laborales, proscripciones y persecución política.
Para Storani, esa combinación era fundamental. Karakachoff tenía una intensa actividad política, pero también ejercía como abogado laboralista. Compartía un estudio con Domingo “Mingo” Teruggi y trabajaba en la defensa de trabajadores y de personas perseguidas por razones políticas. Esa relación profesional terminaría teniendo un peso trágico en su historia.
El golpe de Estado de 1966, que llevó a Juan Carlos Onganía al poder, clausuró el funcionamiento de los partidos políticos y profundizó la radicalización de buena parte de la juventud. En ese contexto, los jóvenes radicales comenzaron a buscar una nueva identidad para una fuerza que consideraban demasiado encerrada en sus estructuras tradicionales.
Karakachoff fue parte de ese proceso. Participó de la construcción de una corriente propia que se expresó en el Movimiento de Afirmación Popular y, posteriormente, en el Movimiento de Renovación y Cambio. El objetivo excedía la disputa de una elección interna: buscaban modificar la relación del radicalismo con la sociedad.
En 1969 apareció En Lucha, una publicación que tuvo a Karakachoff entre sus principales impulsores. El periódico era una herramienta de militancia y de intervención política mientras el régimen militar restringía los canales institucionales. Karakachoff preparaba originales, participaba de la producción y distribución y utilizaba el periodismo como otra forma de hacer política. Escribía, argumentaba y buscaba convencer. Entendía que la construcción política necesitaba también una disputa de ideas.
En paralelo, en 1968 comenzó a organizarse en Santa Fe la Junta Coordinadora Nacional. Reunió a jóvenes dirigentes radicales que compartían una crítica al funcionamiento tradicional del partido y buscaban construir una alternativa generacional. Allí confluyeron figuras como Storani, Luis “Changui” Cáceres, Marcelo y Adolfo Stubrin, Enrique “Coti” Nosiglia, Facundo Suárez Lastra y Mario Losada, entre otros. Karakachoff fue una de sus figuras en La Plata.
Storani recuerda que se conocieron siendo muy jóvenes, a través de Mingo Teruggi. La Coordinadora no nació simplemente como una estructura interna de la UCR; era la expresión de una generación que pretendía sacar al partido de una situación que consideraba de inmovilidad.
El diagnóstico era que el radicalismo tenía una enorme estructura territorial, pero que funcionaba fundamentalmente cuando había elecciones. Fuera de los períodos electorales, según la mirada de aquellos jóvenes, el partido quedaba “dormido”.
La respuesta fue construir otros espacios: frentes de trabajo, presencia universitaria, actividad barrial y vínculos con trabajadores y organizaciones sociales. En La Plata, la militancia universitaria y la relación con sectores obreros fueron una parte importante de aquella experiencia.
La ciudad tenía además una particularidad: era el territorio de Ricardo Balbín, que dominaba buena parte del radicalismo bonaerense. Los jóvenes que después formarían la Coordinadora debieron enfrentarse internamente con una estructura consolidada y perdieron elecciones internas antes de comenzar a crecer y adquirir una dimensión nacional.
Cuando apareció Raúl Alfonsín como una alternativa dentro del radicalismo, la Coordinadora encontró una figura con la que compartía buena parte de ese diagnóstico. “Cuando aparece Alfonsín, nosotros vemos que es lo más próximo a lo que nosotros sentíamos”, recordó Storani. Alfonsín comenzó a participar de actividades organizadas por los jóvenes y, según su relato, llegó a ser detenido durante un acto callejero en La Plata. “Un acto callejero, por supuesto, de su tipo relámpago, como se decía en ese momento; improvisado, con unos cajones y un megáfono.”
Para Storani, la relación fue anterior incluso a la creación de Renovación y Cambio: “La Coordinadora es previa incluso a la fundación del Movimiento Renovación y Cambio, que lo unge a Alfonsín como líder.” Aquella red de jóvenes terminaría convirtiéndose en una de las principales bases de movilización del alfonsinismo y Karakachoff estaba en el centro de ese proceso.
Una generación que discutió cómo enfrentar la violencia. Para entender a Karakachoff también hay que entender aquello que decidió no hacer.
En los años 70, la violencia política se convirtió en uno de los ejes centrales de la vida argentina. La expansión de las organizaciones armadas, la represión estatal y paraestatal y el deterioro de las instituciones llevaron a sectores de la juventud a considerar la lucha armada como un camino posible para transformar el país. Karakachoff rechazó esa alternativa.
Storani insiste en que no se trataba de una posición circunstancial. “Fue absolutamente en contra de la metodología de la violencia”, recuerda. “Su convicción era muy profunda, porque no solamente era desde el punto de vista personal, sino que era política; era un análisis político que hacía”.
La alternativa que defendían era explícita. “En nuestro planteo eran elecciones libres, sin proscripciones y sin condicionamientos”, explicó Storani. Karakachoff rechazaba “el método de la lucha armada como forma –se decía en aquella época–, de asumir la lucha armada para la toma del poder”.
En ese punto se produjo una ruptura con otros sectores juveniles. Storani recuerda una discusión en la sede de la Juventud Política Argentina, donde se anunció la subordinación a la conducción político-militar de Montoneros. La Coordinadora y la Juventud Socialista Popular rechazaron esa decisión.
Para Karakachoff, la democracia no era solamente un objetivo final. Era el método.
Había militantes atraídos por la lucha armada que conversaban con él para intentar convencerlo. Karakachoff hacía el camino inverso: trataba de explicarles por qué consideraba que estaban cometiendo un error. Creía que la violencia terminaría profundizando aquello que pretendía combatir y que una transformación duradera debía construirse desde la política.
“Él era el abogado de los trabajadores, y además comprometido en esa lucha, ese era un poco su rol”, recordó Storani. La militancia del grupo tampoco se limitaba a las estructuras partidarias. “Nuestra militancia también era muy social en esa época”, explicó, al recordar el trabajo con talleres navales, empleados frigoríficos y trabajadores de Berisso, Ensenada y La Plata. “Había mucha efervescencia de la unidad obrero estudiantil, que se expresaba con mucha fuerza”.
Storani recuerda particularmente el trabajo con el ATULP, el sindicato de trabajadores no docentes de la Universidad Nacional de La Plata. Muchos de quienes participaban de aquellas actividades terminarían siendo perseguidos, secuestrados o asesinados durante la dictadura.
El clima político se volvía cada vez más peligroso. “Acá en La Plata el clima era irrespirable”, recordó Storani. “Las bombas sonaban todos los días, los tiroteos también, y quienes asumíamos un compromiso de seguir militando sabíamos que el riesgo era grande. Él también lo sabía”.
Aun así, había momentos en los que entendían que debían hacer alguna demostración pública para mostrar que seguían allí: repartir volantes, hacer pintadas u organizar actividades. Esa decisión tendría una de sus expresiones más dramáticas después del asesinato de Karakachoff, cuando Storani habló desde los balcones de la Casa Radical de la calle 48 durante el funeral de su amigo. Los Falcon verdes pasaban y disparaban.
El abogado que defendía a los perseguidos. A medida que la represión aumentaba, la actividad política de Karakachoff quedó cada vez más vinculada con la defensa de los derechos humanos. En 1975 se incorporó a la Asamblea Permanente por los Derechos Humanos y participó en presentaciones judiciales y habeas corpus vinculados con personas detenidas y perseguidas.
La persecución, sin embargo, no había comenzado en 1976. Cinco años antes, en 1971, Karakachoff ya había sido detenido por su actividad como abogado defensor de presos políticos y trabajadores perseguidos. Storani recuerda que la noticia movilizó inmediatamente a los jóvenes radicales de La Plata.
La respuesta fue una campaña militante. “Pintamos toda la ciudad de La Plata, estuvimos toda la noche pintando ‘Libertad Karakachoff’”. La detención estaba vinculada con su labor como abogado y, según Storani, especialmente con los ferroviarios de La Plata, que atravesaban un período de fuerte conflictividad. “Era por su labor en general, pero yo lo vinculo más que nada en esa oportunidad a esta cuestión de los ferroviarios que estaban en lucha”, explicó.
La cercanía con esos trabajadores formaba parte de una concepción de la militancia que excedía la vida interna de un partido. La política también estaba en los sindicatos, las universidades y los conflictos sociales. La Unión Ferroviaria de La Plata tenía además un secretario general radical, un vínculo que reforzaba la relación con aquellos jóvenes militantes.
La detención de 1971 fue una experiencia temprana de persecución política. Antes de convertirse en una víctima del terrorismo de Estado, Karakachoff ya había conocido la privación de la libertad como consecuencia de su actividad profesional y política.
La represión que siguió al golpe del 24 de marzo de 1976 agravó todavía más la situación. La familia sabía que había peligro y comenzó a tomar precauciones, aunque Matilde, que tenía cuatro años, era demasiado chica para comprenderlo.
Con los años, una de las preguntas que más la acompañó fue cómo podía alguien que conocía el nivel de riesgo continuar adelante. Su madre siempre sostuvo que Sergio sabía lo que podía pasar y que no había sido ingenuo. Una amiga de la familia, Ana, una de las últimas personas que habló con él, le había advertido durante los días anteriores que la situación era cada vez más peligrosa.
El 10 de septiembre, sus hijas no fueron a la guardería que compartían con sus primos. A la salida, una maestra advirtió a la tía de las niñas: “Mirá que unos tipos vinieron a preguntar por Matilde y Sofía”. La familia se movió inmediatamente a una casa de confianza, pero Sergio decidió ir antes hasta la vivienda de Mingo Teruggi.
Para Matilde, ese dato modificó la forma de pensar sus últimos minutos. Durante mucho tiempo se preguntó cómo podía no haber visto el peligro. Después empezó a pensar que quizá sí lo había visto. Su madre siempre sostuvo que decidió correr el riesgo y que no habría querido dejar solo a Mingo.
Sergio estaba trabajando en su oficina, cerca de la casa familiar. Dijo que iría detrás de ellos, pero antes quería pasar por la casa de Teruggi. Ese fue el último trayecto que hizo. Cuando llegó, los represores ya estaban allí. Nunca volvió.
El 10 de septiembre de 1976. Sergio Karakachoff fue secuestrado el 10 de septiembre de 1976 en La Plata junto a Domingo “Mingo” Teruggi. Ambos fueron trasladados y torturados. Sus cuerpos aparecieron al día siguiente cerca de la Ruta 36, en la zona de General Mansilla, partido de Magdalena. Karakachoff tenía 37 años.
Teruggi era su amigo, compañero de militancia y colega. La relación entre ambos había comenzado en los espacios de la política universitaria y radical y después habían trabajado juntos como abogados.
Para Matilde, la muerte de su padre quedó durante años como una certeza sin imágenes. No recuerda el secuestro ni la violencia. Su primera memoria relacionada con aquel episodio es otra: la llegada a Venezuela en diciembre de 1976, tres meses después del asesinato.
La familia debió exiliarse. Marimé Arias, la esposa de Sergio, estuvo inicialmente refugiada en la Embajada de Venezuela y después viajó como refugiada política. La familia se instaló allí y posteriormente pasó un largo período en Roma.
Storani mantuvo el contacto durante ese tiempo y viajaba a Italia para colaborar con la familia y con la Fundación Sergio Karakachoff, creada en Argentina en homenaje al dirigente. Marimé tenía un papel central en esa tarea y organizaba parte de sus actividades y contactos, especialmente con sindicatos y organizaciones políticas.
Matilde volvió a Argentina siendo niña, pero su madre no podía acompañarla. Ella y su hermana quedaron al cuidado de una tía en una quinta de Hernández. Incluso entonces existía una regla que de niña no terminaba de comprender: no debían decir su apellido.
Con el tiempo entendió que el peligro no había terminado con la muerte de Sergio, sino que se había trasladado a la vida cotidiana de quienes llevaban su apellido.
La familia recibió ayuda de amigos y antiguos compañeros de militancia. Llegaban visitas, regalos, mates y conversaciones.
