इतिहासकारहरूबीच मतान्तर रहे पनि नवपाषाण युगका मानिस, नाग जाति हुँदै मल्लकालसम्म आएका विभिन्न राजवंश, उनीहरूसित आएका जनता र अनेक शरणार्थीको मिश्रणबाट एकाकार भई विकास र विस्तार हुँदै आएको समुदाय रहेकाले उपत्यकाको विस्तार क्रम र विस्तारकर्मीहरूबारे लेखिएको हो। उपत्यकाबाट बसाइँ सरी गएकाहरूबारे पनि भेटेसम्म ऐतिहासिकता खोजिएको छ।
नेवारहरू आफैँले वर्षभरि मनाउने कुनै न कुनै चाडपर्व र जात्राहरूमा परम्परा अनुसार मुकुन्डोनाच प्रस्तुत गर्छन्।
हालसम्म मुकुन्डोनाच जातीय जिम्मेवारीका आधारमा सञ्चालन हुँदै आएको छ। यस कारण नेवारहरूको जातीय वर्गीकरण, जातका नाम, उपनाम, पेसा आदि उल्लेख गरिएको हो। नाचका सबै काम गुठीबाट सञ्चालन हुने भएकाले गुठी व्यवस्थाबारे पनि जानकारी दिइएको छ।
नेपाल उपत्यकामाथि विजय हासिल गरेपछि गोर्खाली राजा पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले देशको नामै नेपाल राखी राजधानी पनि यहीँ सारे। त्यसपछि नेपाल अधिराज्यमा बसोबास गर्ने सबै नेपालीको राजधानी काठमाडौँ भयो। यहाँ अन्य जनजातिका नाचगान प्रदर्शन र राजनीतिक मोडसँगै देशविदेशका नाचका प्रशिक्षण केन्द्र, महाविद्यालय, सरकारी सङ्घ-संस्था तथा त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालयमा सङ्गीत-नृत्य अध्ययन हुन थालेको इतिहास पनि नेवार समुदायको मुकुन्डोनाचको रङ्गभूमिमै थपिएका आयाम हुन्। नृत्यको इतिहासमा थपिँदै गएका यी नयाँ आयामबारे पहिलो खण्डमै प्रकाश पारिएको छ।
नेवारहरू आफैँले वर्षभरि मनाउने कुनै न कुनै चाडपर्व र जात्राहरूमा परम्परा अनुसार मुकुन्डोनाच प्रस्तुत गर्छन्। यस कारण दोस्रो खण्डमा नेवारहरूले मनाउने प्रमुख चाडपर्व, जात्रा र उपलक्ष्य आदिको परिचय चन्द्रमासिक गणनाका तिथि अनुसार र सूर्यमासिक गणनाका महिनाहरूबाट गराइएको छ। खास गरी प्रत्येक नेवार गाउँ वा नगरको जात्रामा भएका नाचसहित स्थानीय बाजागाजा, भजनमा सामूहिक सहभागिता हुने भएकाले जात्रा धार्मिक उत्सवजस्तै देखिए पनि स्थानीय नाट्य-सङ्गीतको उत्सव पनि हो। यस कारण नेवार समुदायले मनाउने चाडपर्व र स्थानीय जात्राबारे संक्षेपमा जानकारी गराइएको हो। यसक्रममा कुनै नाच प्रस्तुत गरिने उत्सव र स्थानीय जात्राहरू छुटेका भए क्षमा चाहन्छु।
केही मुकुन्डोनाचमा जन्मदेखि मृत्युपछिका संस्कारहरू पनि गर्नुपर्छ। यस कारण हिन्दू तथा बौद्ध नेवार परम्पराको परिचय दिएर नेवारहरूको प्रमुख संस्कारबारे संक्षेपमा लेखिएको हो। हाम्रा यी संस्कारका विधिविधान हिजोआज छोट्याएर प्रमुख विधि मात्र गर्न थालिएकाले इतिहासकै रूपमा भए पनि अभिलेख सञ्चय गर्नु उद्देश्य रहेको छ।
उपत्यकामा मातृका पूजनको आरम्भकालको लेखाजोखा र यहाँ भेटिएका प्राचीन मूर्तिहरूबाट पनि मुकुन्डोनाचको सम्भावित इतिहासबारे खोज्ने प्रयास गरिएको छ।
तेस्रो खण्डमा ‘नाचका पात्रहरू’ को परिचय गराउने क्रममा हनुमान्नाचबाहेक प्रायः सबै मुकुन्डोनाचका मूल पात्र शक्ति सम्प्रदायका त्रिमहाशक्ति र अष्टमातृका भैरवगण पूर्ण वा विभिन्न सङ्ख्यामा रहेकाले सङ्कलनमा रहेका प्रत्येक मुकुन्डोनाचका पात्रको सूची दिइएको हो। त्रिमहाशक्तिलाई नृत्यसिद्धि प्रदान गर्ने नासःद्यः स्वरूप र अष्टमातृका भैरवगणलाई अष्टसिद्धि प्रदान गर्ने रङ्गपीठ देवता मानेर नाचमा पूजिन्छ। नासःद्यःको पूजा आआफ्नो परम्परा अनुसार नगरी नाचको तालिम सुरु हुँदैन। अर्धतान्त्रिक नाचहरूमा अष्टमातृकाको शक्तिसाधना पूजा पनि नासःद्यःको जस्तै गर्नुपर्छ। नाचको परम्परा र हिन्दू तथा बौद्ध तन्त्रको मत अनुसार पात्रहरूको बाह्य र गुह्य रूप फरक हुन्छन्। तन्त्रमा वास्तविकतालाई गोप्य राखिने हुँदा नासःद्यः र अष्टमातृका भैरवगणको बाह्य र गुह्य परिचय, स्थापित स्थान, तन्त्रमा यिनको साङ्केतिक रूपरङ, बौद्धमार्गी तथा हिन्दूहरूको आआफ्नो मार्ग अनुसार साङ्केतिक अर्थ र यिनका स्थापित पीठहरू, यिनको बाह्य र गोप्य नाम आदिबारे तन्त्राचार्यहरूले गरेको व्याख्याका आधारमा चिनाउने प्रयास गरिएको छ।
उपत्यकामा मातृका पूजनको आरम्भकालको लेखाजोखा र यहाँ भेटिएका प्राचीन मूर्तिहरूबाट पनि मुकुन्डोनाचको सम्भावित इतिहासबारे खोज्ने प्रयास गरिएको छ। तलेजु भवानी अष्टमातृकाभित्र नपरे पनि प्रत्येक नाचले अष्टमातृका संयुक्त रूप वा ज्येष्ठ दिदीस्वरूप मान्ने भएकाले यिनको उपत्यकामा आगमन र मल्ल राजदरबारमा स्थापनाको इतिहास संक्षेपमा लेखिएको छ।
चौथो खण्डमा शास्त्रीय नृत्यका ‘प्रविधि र प्रस्तुति प्रकरण’ दिइएको छ। नेवारहरूमा मुकुन्डोनाचको धार्मिक भावनासँगै एकातिर तन्त्रसाधनाको मार्ग मानिएको छ भने अर्कोतिर केही मुकुन्डोनाचमा प्रयोग भएका प्रविधि भरतको नाट्यशास्त्र र नन्दीकेश्वरको अभिनयदर्पणमा व्याख्या गरिएको शास्त्रीय नृत्यमा हुनुपर्ने मूल प्रविधि अङ्गीकार गरिएको पाइन्छ। तर, यिनको प्रविधिसम्बन्धी ग्रन्थ अहिलेसम्म भेट्न नसकिएकाले यिनै शास्त्रका आधारमा प्रत्येक मुकुन्डोनाचको शास्त्रीयता मूल्याङ्कन गरिएको छ।
पाँचौँदेखि सत्रौँ खण्डसम्म एउटै नाम र समान प्रस्तुति प्रकरण भएका मुकुन्डोनाचलाई एकै खण्डमा अध्याय विभाजन गरी लेखिएको छ। गणना गर्दा चालीस नाघे पनि सबै परम्परागत मुकुन्डोनाच नसमेटिएका हुन सक्छन्। अघिल्ला चार खण्डमा उल्लेख गरिएका विषयवस्तुका आधारमा प्रत्येक नाचको इतिहास, रङ्गशाला (नाचिने स्थान), त्यहाँ बसोबास गर्ने नेवार, प्रमुख चाडपर्व, जात्रा, रङ्गकर्मी, नाच सञ्चालन गर्ने गुठी, समिति, सहभागी पात्र, जातीय सहभागिता, नाचको प्रविधि, पूजा, प्रस्तुति प्रकरण एवं आजको स्थिति र आर्थिक अवस्थाबारे जानकारी दिइएको छ।
धार्मिक क्षेत्रमा चर्यानृत्यको प्रस्तुति पूजाको अभ्यन्तर विधि मानिए पनि शास्त्रीय नृत्य प्रविधि आफ्नै पद्धति अनुसार प्रयोग भएको देखिन्छ।
पाँचौँ खण्डमा चर्यानर्तन पद्धतिको इतिहास, प्रस्तुति र आधुनिक रङ्गमञ्च यसको प्रस्तुतिका तीन क्षेत्र छुट्याइएको छ।
धार्मिक क्षेत्रबाटै चर्यानृत्यको इतिहास आरम्भ भएकाले बौद्धयानहरूको परिचय, यिनको उदयकाल, चर्याको परिभाषा, गुरुशिष्यको गोप्य परम्परा, सिद्धकाल, श्लोकस्तोत्र र तन्त्रका आधारमा चर्यानृत्यको प्रारम्भिक इतिहास एवं प्रस्तुतिबारे संक्षेपमै भए पनि प्राचीनता खोज्ने प्रयास गरिएको छ। नेपाल उपत्यकामा धार्मिक क्षेत्रमा चर्यानृत्यको अभ्यास र अवस्था भेटेसम्म बौद्ध ग्रन्थ, अभिलेख, वंशावली, विद्वान्हरूका मत, नाचका केही परम्परा, चर्यागायनमा उल्लिखित केही रचनाकारहरूको समय, चर्यागीत रचेर गएका सिद्धहरू, चर्यागायन र नृत्यमा योगदान पुर्याएका वज्राचार्य गुरुहरू, तिनले रचेका पूजामा गाइने चर्यागीत र धार्मिक क्षेत्रमा चर्यानृत्यको प्राचीन इतिहास जोडेर हेर्ने कोसिस गरिएको छ। धार्मिक क्षेत्रमा चर्यानृत्य प्रस्तुत हुने उदाहरणका निमित्त वज्रवाराही र कुरकुल्लादेवीको मण्डलका चक्रका दिशा दिशामा रहने देवीको नाम, वर्ण, अङ्गभङ्गीसहित परिचय गराइएको छ।
धार्मिक क्षेत्रमा चर्यानृत्यको प्रस्तुति पूजाको अभ्यन्तर विधि मानिए पनि शास्त्रीय नृत्य प्रविधि आफ्नै पद्धति अनुसार प्रयोग भएको देखिन्छ। प्रत्येक चर्यागीत राग र तालमा बन्देज गरिएका छन्। देवदेवीहरूको स्थान, अङ्गभङ्गी, हस्तमुद्रा, पदस्थान, धर्मधातु मण्डलका आधारमा व्याख्या गरिएको छ। दीक्षित वज्राचार्य गुरुहरूले मात्र धार्मिक क्षेत्रका पूजामा सहभागी हुने र नाच्ने अधिकार भएकाले दीक्षाबारे संक्षेपमा जानकारी गराइएको हो। ललितपुर र कान्तिपुरमा पूजामा गाइने र नाचिने चर्यागीतका नाम, राग, तालसँगै केही रचनाकार पनि उल्लेख गर्ने कोसिस भएको छ। मेरा विभिन्न गुरुहरूको सहयोग पाएकैले चर्यानर्तन पद्धतिका तीनै क्षेत्रमा हुँदै आएको प्रस्तुतिको आरम्भ र विस्तारको इतिहास, प्रविधि र प्रस्तुतिबारे लेख्न सकिएको हो। यसबारे अझ विस्तृत शोध गरी चर्यानृत्यको शास्त्रीयता अभ्यासमा ल्याउनु आवश्यक देखिन्छ।
चर्याशैलीमा आधारित दबूप्याखंहरूको आरम्भ मल्लकालमा भएको हो। यसै शैलीमा आधारित दुई नाच काठमाडौँमा नाचिन्थ्यो तर केही दशकअघि बन्द भइसके पनि इतिहासको सम्झनामा लेखिएको हो। ललितपुरमा नाचिने गंप्याखं यही शैलीमा आधारित छ। चर्यागुरु आशाकाजी पण्डितकी शिष्याको नाताले गंप्याखँ सिक्नुका साथै यसको इतिहास, प्रविधि, प्रस्तुतिबारे प्राप्त जानकारीका साथै अवलोकनका आधारमा लेखिएको हो। चर्यानृत्यको प्रस्तुतिको तेस्रो क्षेत्र आधुनिक रङ्गमञ्चमा प्रस्तुति तथा प्रशिक्षण २०१३ सालदेखि दीक्षित वज्राचार्य गुरुहरूले नै आरम्भ गरेको नयाँ आयाम हो। चर्यानृत्य प्रदर्शनकारी कलासम्बद्ध सरकारी तथा निजी सङ्घ-संस्थामा प्रशिक्षण र प्रदर्शनदेखि विश्वविद्यालयका पाठ्यक्रम र देशविदेशमा हुँदै आएका प्रस्तुतिको आरम्भिक इतिहासबारे चर्चा गरिएको छ।
देवीनाचको इतिहास, रङ्गकर्मी, प्रविधि, प्रस्तुति, आजको अवस्था र आर्थिक व्यवस्थाबारे अरू मुकुन्डोनाचमा जस्तै गरी लेखिए पनि उदाहरणका रूपमा किलागलको देवीनाचबारे विस्तृत व्याख्या गरिएको हो।
छैटौँ खण्डमा गथुप्याखंबारे लेखिएको छ। नेपाल भाषामा मालाकार जातिलाई गथु भन्छन्। यो जातिले मात्र नाच्ने मुकुन्डोनाच भएकाले यसलाई गथुप्याखं भनिएको हो। गथुप्याखंका समूह भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा एक एक भए पनि कान्तिपुरमा तीन वटा छन्। कान्तिपुरको एक समूहले दुइटा नाच सञ्चालन गर्दै आएकाले पाँच वटा नाचलाई चार अध्यायमा विभाजन गरिएको छ। कान्तिपुरको पचली भैरव र भद्रकालीनाचको इतिहास, रङ्गकर्मी, प्रविधि, पूजा र नाचपक्ष, समापन विधि र आर्थिक अवस्था दिइएको छ। यही प्रकरणमा भक्तपुरको नवदुर्गानाच, ललितपुरको इन्द्रायणी अथवा नवदुर्गानाच र कीर्तिपुरको वाघभैरव भनिने इन्द्रायणी नाचबारे पनि लेखिएको छ।
सातौँ खण्डमा ललितपुर, कान्तिपुर र चित्लाङका कार्तिकनाचबारे लेखिएको छ। ललितपुर र कान्तिपुरको फर्पिङमा कार्तिकनाचका एकएक समूह छन् तर मकवानपुरको चित्लाङ क्षेत्रमा यसका विभिन्न समूह छन्। कार्तिक महिनामा नचाउन सुरु गरिने भएकाले यिनलाई कार्तिकनाच भनिएको पनि हुन सक्छ। फर्पिङ र चित्लाङमा कार्तिकनाचकै पद्धतिमा नचाइने अरू मुकुन्डोनाच र नृत्यनाट्य पनि छन्। केही नेवार समुदायमा विभिन्न लोकनाच पनि नचाउने परम्परा छ। ललितपुरको कार्तिकनाच मल्ल राजा सिद्धिनरसिंहको पालामा आरम्भ भएको इतिहास छ तर अन्य ठाउँका कार्तिकनाचको इतिहासबारे प्रस्ट अभिलेख भेटिँदैन। प्रत्येक बाह्र वर्षमा नचाइने फर्पिङको दक्षिणकाली नाच र टिस्टुङको वज्रवाराही नाच पनि कार्तिकनाच शैलीमा प्रस्तुत गरिने भएकाले यही खण्डमा दिइएको छ।
आठौँ खण्डमा विभिन्न ठाउँमा नचाइने नौ वटा देवीनाचको चर्चा गरिएको छ। हुन त नेवार समुदायका प्रायः सबै मुकुन्डोनाच मातृका भैरवगण परिवारका कुनै न कुनै मातृका र भैरवको नाममा समर्पण गरिएको हुन्छ। मातृकाहरूलाई देवी पनि भनिन्छ तर सिधै मातृका परिवारको नाम नदिएर केही नाचमा उपनाम मात्र दिइएकाले प्रख्यात देवीनाचबारे मात्र सङ्कलन गरिएको हो।
देवीनाचको इतिहास, रङ्गकर्मी, प्रविधि, प्रस्तुति, आजको अवस्था र आर्थिक व्यवस्थाबारे अरू मुकुन्डोनाचमा जस्तै गरी लेखिए पनि उदाहरणका रूपमा किलागलको देवीनाचबारे विस्तृत व्याख्या गरिएको हो। किलागल टोलको संरचना, स्थानीय नेवारहरूले वर्षभरि मनाउने चाडपर्व र जात्रामा भजन गाउने र बाजा बजाउने परम्परागत व्यवस्था र दायित्व, स्थानीय मठमन्दिर, नासःद्यः र गल्लीहरू नाच्दै परिक्रमा गर्ने परम्परा उल्लेख गरी प्राचीन नेवार बस्तीमा स्थानीय सङ्गीतका रङ्गशाला र परम्परागत गुरुकुल बुझाउन खोजिएको छ।
लोप भइसकेको थैबको देवीनाचको इतिहास खोज्ने प्रयास अभिलेखीकरण नमुना मान्नुहुनेछ।
किलागल र साँखुको देवीनाच मूल रूपले समान भए पनि साँखुमा दैत्यसंहार लीला छैन भने साँगाको देवीनाचमा छोटो नाट्यसंवाद र सप्तमातृका भैरवको प्रमुख नृत्य प्रस्तुति हुन्। पनौतीको देवीनाचमा भैरव र गणेशका साथै महाकाली, वाराही, कुमारी, विष्णुदेवी, ब्रह्मायणी, इन्द्रायणी एवं एक मातृकाको नाम देवी मात्र भनिएको छ। यी मातृका महालक्ष्मी हुन् वा इन्द्रायणी ? नाचका गुरुहरूबीच मतैक्य छैन। काठमाडौँमा पर्ने प्राचीन नगर कीर्तिपुरको देवीनाच पहिले यही मञ्चन गरिने लालहीरा खःप्याखंमा नचाइने गरेको थियो। खःप्याखं बन्द भएपछि छुट्टै देखाउन थालियो।
लोप भइसकेको थैबको देवीनाचको इतिहास खोज्ने प्रयास अभिलेखीकरण नमुना मान्नुहुनेछ। त्यसै गरी झन्डै सय वर्षअघि नै लोप भइसकेको बनेपाको देवीनाचलाई कसैले देवी र कसैले कुमारीनाच भनेका छन्। यसको ऐतिहासिक जानकारी दिन खोजिएको हो। दाप्चा (क्षेत्रवास) को माथिल्लो र तल्लो हटियामा नचाइने क्रमशः देवीभैरवनाच र देवीनाचलाई नवदुर्गानाच पनि भनिन्छ। यी दुवै देवीनाच दाप्चा क्षेत्रवासको माथिल्लो र तल्लो भागमा बसोबास गर्ने नेवारहरूले कृष्ण जन्माष्टमीको उपलक्ष्यमा नचाउँदै आए पनि यिनको इतिहास, प्रस्तुति, व्यवस्थापन बेग्लाबेग्लै भएकाले अध्याय छुट्याएर लेखिएको छ। भोजपुरको टक्सारमा बसोबास गर्ने नेवार समुदायले सर्वसिद्ध खःप्याखंमा नचाउने गरेको देवीनाच छुट्टै नचाउने गरिएको छ। विगतको द्वन्द्वको मारमा परी स्थानीय नेवारहरू बसाइँ सरेपछि यस नाचमा पनि प्रभाव परेको देखिन्छ।
नेवार समुदायको परम्परागत मुकुन्डोनाचमध्ये अर्को आयाम थप्ने महाकालीनाच नवौँ खण्डमा लेखिएको छ। महाकालीनाचका भक्तपुरमा छ समूह र थिमिमा तीन समूह देखिन्छन्। महाकालीनाच एउटै समूहबाट विभाजन भई विभिन्न समूह बनेका हुन्। मल्लकालदेखि नचाइँदै आएको कोलासुरबधोपाख्यान दैत्य खःप्याखंमा नचाइने गरेको देवीनाचलाई राजा सुरेन्द्रविक्रमको शासनकालमा परिमार्जन गरी महाकालीनाच नाम दिएर मनोरञ्जनका रूपमा सुरु गरिएको थियो। एउटैबाट विस्तार हुँदै गएकाले महाकालीनाचको प्रविधि र प्रस्तुति समान छ। यस नाचको आरम्भ र विस्तारले नेवार समुदायको परम्परागत मुकुन्डोनाचमा नयाँ आयाम थपिएको छ।
दशौँ खण्डमा भक्तपुर, बोद्यगाउँको नीलवाराहीनाचबारे लेखिएको छ। एक भैरव, चार गणेश, चार वाराही, चार सिंहिनी, चार कुमारी र दुई द्वारपाल पात्र भएकाले नीलवाराहीनाच छुट्टै रहस्यमय परम्परा बोकेको एवं छ थरी श्रेष्ठले नाच्ने गरेको एक मात्र नाच हो। अरू नाचभन्दा भिन्नै प्रस्तुतीकरण, स्यालले सिकाएको मान्यता र देवघर परिवर्तन गरिरहने यस नाचको विशेषता हो।
एघारौँ खण्डमा भक्तपुरका मूलवासीले भिन्नाभिन्नै तीन ठाउँमा भिन्नाभिन्नै तरिकाले नचाइने भैरवनाचबारे लेखिएको छ। पुरानो नेपाल भाषामा ‘र’ लाई ‘ल’ उच्चारण गरिने भएकाले भक्तपुर र थिमिमा भैलप्याखं भनिन्छ भने पोखरामा नेपाली भाषा प्रभावित भई भैरवनाच वा बाह भैरवनाच भनिन्छ। यी तीनै ठाउँमा भैरवनाच भनिए पनि नाचिने प्रकरण र पात्रको सङ्ख्या भिन्नाभिन्नै भएकाले अध्याय छुट्याएर लेखिएको हो।
रुद्रायणी मन्दिरको स्वामित्व भएको यो नाचमा पूजा र नाचको दायित्व निश्चित गुठीमा रहे पनि खोकनाका अन्य गुठीहरूले सहयोग गर्ने परम्परा छ।
बाह्रौँ खण्डमा कान्तिपुरका प्राचीन नगरभित्र पर्ने नरदेवीको श्वेतकालीनाचबारे लेखिएको छ। नेपाल भाषामा यसलाई ङ्यतमरु अजिमा भनिन्छ। यस नाचमा श्वेतकालीको अहम् भूमिका भए पनि दैत्यसंहार गर्ने नायिका कुमारीको चण्डीरूप हुन्। काली भन्नाले रातो वा कालो वर्णकी भन्ने बुझिन्छ तर यो नाचकी काली श्वेत वर्णकी छन्। यो नाचमा मात्रै नेवार समुदायबाहेक पाण्डे, झा, भट्ट आदिले मन्दिरको पूजा र नाचको निरन्तरताका लागि गुठी स्थापना गरेको पाइन्छ।
तेह्रौँ खण्डमा ललितपुरमा पर्ने जलगाउँको ‘जलप्याखं’ अर्थात् हरसिद्धिनाचबारे लेखिएको छ। हरसिद्धिनाचलाई नेपाल उपत्यकामा अहिलेसम्म सञ्चालित सबैभन्दा प्राचीन मुकुन्डोनाच मानिन्छ। विक्रमादित्य र चालुक्य वंशसँग सम्बद्ध यो नाचमा प्रवेश गरेपछि मन्दिरको पूजा गर्ने च्याभूहरू कपाल र जुँघादाह्री नकाटी श्वेतवस्त्रमा जीवन यापन गर्ने परम्परा कायम छ। यसमा प्रस्तुत गरिने नृत्यनाट्य वैष्णव र शैवमतमा आधारित भएकाले ‘हर’ र ‘हरि’ दुवै नाम प्रचलनमा आएको बुझिन्छ।
चौधौँ खण्डमा ललितपुरकै खोकनाको ‘सिकालीप्याखँ’ (सिद्धिकाली) अर्थात् रुद्रायणीनाचबारे लेखिएको छ। रुद्रायणी मन्दिरको स्वामित्व भएको यो नाचमा पूजा र नाचको दायित्व निश्चित गुठीमा रहे पनि खोकनाका अन्य गुठीहरूले सहयोग गर्ने परम्परा छ। सिद्धिकालीनाचमा कपाल र जुँघादाह्री नकाटे पनि मन्दिरको पूजा र नाचमा बाहेक श्वेतवस्त्र लाउनु पर्दैन। स्वस्थानीको कथामा आधारित रहेकाले पनि यसलाई रुद्रायणीनाच भनिएको हुन सक्छ। रुद्रायणी देवी शाकाहारी मानिन्छिन्। त्यसैले रुद्रायणी देवीलाई समर्पण गरिएको सिद्धिकालीनाचमा दैत्यबध लीला महालक्ष्मीले गर्छिन्।
पन्ध्रौँ खण्डमा प्राचीन नगर कान्तिपुर क्षेत्रमा पर्ने हलचोकका पुतवारहरूले प्रत्येक वर्ष नाच्दै आएको सवःभकु अर्थात् आकाशभैरवनाचबारे लेखिएको छ। लोकधर्मितामा आधारित साधारण ताल बाजामा मात्र नाचिने भए पनि आकाशभैरवनाचमा प्रत्येक बाह्र वर्षमा केही पात्र थपेर नयाँ वर्षको उपलक्ष्यमा नचाइन्छ। प्रस्तुति साधारण देखिए पनि यो नाच नाच्दै आएका पुतवारबारे प्रचलित भ्रामक जनश्रुतिले हालसम्म यिनीहरूबारे नलेखिएको इतिहास खोज्न प्रयास गरिएको छ।
‘केही नाच नभएको ठाउँमा लाखय् नाच भए पनि नचाउनु’ भन्ने मान्यता भएको नेवार समुदायमा आआफ्नो परम्परा अनुसार विभिन्न समूहले नाच्दै आएको लाखय् नाचबारे सोह्रौँ खण्डमा लेखिएको छ। हिजोआज त भारत, अमेरिका, युरोपतिर बसाइँ सरेका नेवारहरूले पनि नचाउन थालेका छन्। सबै ठाउँमा नचाइने लाखय् नाचबारे लेख्न सम्भव भएन। लाखय्लाई कतै मानव जातिलाई धन र सुरक्षा दिने दैवी शक्ति भएको तलेजु भवानीको अङ्गरक्षक मानिन्छ भने कतै नकारात्मक पात्र दैत्यका रूपमा हेरिन्छ। काठमाडौँको मजिपाः लाखय्लाई सकारात्मक मानिन्छ। सबैभन्दा पुरानो लाखय् नाच मानिएकाले यसबारे विस्तारपूर्वक लेखिएको हो।
सत्रौँ वा अन्तिम खण्डमा भक्तपुरको माकःप्याखं र बाग्लुङको हनुमान्नाचबारे लेखिएको छ। भक्तपुरबाट बेनी र कुस्मासम्म पुगेको हनुमान्नाचबारे पनि संक्षिप्त चिनारी यसैमा जोडिएको छ। नाचको प्रस्तुति प्रकरण मूल रूपले समान देखिए पनि नाच्ने ठाउँ र नाचको नाम बेग्लाबेग्लै भएकाले अध्याय छुट्याइएको हो। प्रायः सबै मुकुन्डोनाचमा पात्र र सिद्धि दिने देवदेवीहरू शक्ति सम्प्रदायमा आधारित छन्। हनुमान् पात्र सो सम्प्रदायमा नभए पनि नर्तकहरूलाई सुस्वास्थ्य दिने देवताका रूपमा पूजिन्छ। यस कारण यिनको पनि नाच रचिएको हुन सक्छ। शारीरिक शान्ति दिने सात्त्विक देवता मानिएकाले माकःप्याखं वा हनुमान्मा समर्पित यो नाच अन्तिम खण्डमा राखिएको हो।
२०२६ देखि ८२ सम्म नाच खोजीको ५६ वर्षे यात्रामा नाच प्रस्तुतिसित जोडिएका सूचना, जानकारी दिने र इतिहास रच्ने पात्रहरूसँग गरिएका अन्तर्वार्ता निकै सहयोगी रहे।
यसरी यस पुस्तकमा समेटिएका प्रत्येक मुकुन्डोनाचको सैद्धान्तिक (परिचयात्मक वा ऐतिहासिक) र प्रायोगिक (प्रविधि र प्रस्तुति) पक्षसित जोडिएका इतिहास, मूल रङ्गभूमि, विविध रङ्गशाला, नाचिने क्षेत्र, रङ्गकर्मी र तिनको कार्य विभाजनबारे विस्तृत व्याख्या गर्ने कोसिस गरिएको छ। यस क्रममा प्रायः सबै नाचको प्रस्तुति अवलोकन गरी प्रविधि, पूजा र नृत्य समेटिएका छन्। बन्द भइसकेका नाचबारेका सूचना विविध व्यक्ति, क्षेत्र र अभिलेखहरूबाट लिइएको हो। नेवार समुदायका मुकुन्डोनाच खोज्ने क्रमको यति लामो यात्रामा सहयोगीहरूको नाम छुटेका भए क्षमा चाहन्छु।
२०२६ देखि ८२ सम्म नाच खोजीको ५६ वर्षे यात्रामा नाच प्रस्तुतिसित जोडिएका सूचना, जानकारी दिने र इतिहास रच्ने पात्रहरूसँग गरिएका अन्तर्वार्ता निकै सहयोगी रहे। वि.सं. २०१० मा स्थापित ‘भैरव नृत्यदल’ का संस्थापक भैरवबहादुर थापा, २०११ मा पहिलोपल्ट काठमाडौँ उपत्यकामा मलङ्गवा हाइस्कुलका छात्रछात्राले ल्याएको सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रम प्रस्तुत गराउने टोलीका संयोजक रामहरि जोशी र तत्कालीन सहभागी छात्रछात्रा, २०१३ मा पहिलोपल्ट आधुनिक रङ्गमञ्च (नारायणहिटी दरबार) मा चर्यानृत्य प्रस्तुत गर्नेमध्ये सप्तमुनि बज्राचार्य, सोही वर्ष नेवार लोकनाचहरू आधुनिक रङ्गमञ्चमा पहिलोपल्ट प्रस्तुत गर्ने सौभाग्यवती रञ्जितकार, आधुनिक मञ्चमा पहिलोपल्ट महिलालाई चर्यानृत्य प्रस्तुत गराउने चैत्यराज बज्राचार्य, प्रथम नृत्याङ्गना शान्ति कंसाकार हुन्।
त्यसै गरी वि.सं. २०१६ मा काठमाडौँमा भारतीय शास्त्रीय प्रशिक्षण केन्द्र खोल्ने पहिलो महिला सुशीला कोइराला, वि.सं. २०२० मा स्थापित भारत विद्यापीठ (लखनउ) बारे बताउने सुशीला अमात्य, सोही वर्ष नेपाल राजकीय प्रज्ञा-प्रतिष्ठानमा नृत्यसित आबद्ध नारायणदेवी प्रधान, संस्कृति विभागको स्थापनादेखि सांस्कृतिक संस्थानसम्म जोडिएका राममान प्रधान, वि.सं. २०२६ मा पद्मकन्या कलेजको मानविकी सङ्कायअन्तर्गत नृत्य विषय पाठ्यक्रममा राख्ने पहिलो क्याम्पस प्रमुख अङ्गुरबाबा जोशी हुन्।
नयाँ आयाम थप्ने व्यक्तिहरूसित अन्तर्वार्ता लिएर लेख्न पाएकाले उहाँहरूको सहयोगलाई शब्दमा कृतज्ञता जाहेर गर्नु थोरै हुन्छ। नेपालमा प्रजातन्त्र पुनर्बहालीपछि वि.सं. २०४८-०५० मा शिक्षा, संस्कृति तथा पर्यटन मन्त्रालयको संयुक्त आयोजनामा काठमाडौँमा इन्द्रजात्रामा नचाइने मुकुन्डोनाचहरू हनुमान्ढोकाभित्र, मध्यपहाडी भूभागका लोकनाचहरूको प्रतियोगिता पोखरामा भए। चितवनमा पूर्वदेखि पश्चिमसम्म बसोबास गर्ने थारूहरूका लोकनाच र जनकपुरको जानकी मन्दिरभित्र मिथिला लोकसङ्गीत एवं नृत्यनाट्यका प्रतियोगिता उनैका स्थानमा संयोजन गरेकी थिएँ। यी चारै ठाउँका प्रतियोगिताबाट उत्कृष्ट छानिएका नाचहरू फिनल्यान्ड, जर्मनी, जापान आदि देशमा सांस्कृतिक पर्यटनको प्रचारका लागि लगिएको थियो। यिनै अनुभवका आधारमा २०५८ सालदेखि पर्यटन मन्त्रालयले आयोजना गर्ने गरेको स्थानीय परम्परागत लोकनाचहरूबारे थोरै भए पनि जोड्न सकियो। यो प्रजातन्त्र पुनर्बहालीसँगै नेपाल सरकारबाट स्थानीय परम्परागत मुकुन्डोनाच, लोकनाच र जातीय मौलिक नाच प्रचारमा ल्याउन गरेको प्रयासमा संयोजक हुन पाउँदा नेपालको केही प्रमुख जनजातिका लोकनाचबारे अध्ययन गर्न पाउनु मेरो लागि ठुलो उपलब्धि थियो। सरकारी संस्थाबाट नृत्य विषयमा भएका अनुसन्धानमूलक काम सर्वसाधारणको जानकारीका निम्ति नेपाल राजकीय प्रज्ञा-प्रतिष्ठान, नेपाल सङ्गीत नाट्य प्रज्ञा-प्रतिष्ठान र सांस्कृतिक संस्थानले स्थापनाकालदेखि नृत्य विषयमा गरेका कार्यक्रमबारे तिनै संस्थाका बुलेटिनको सहयोग लिइयो। पर्यटन विभागले पछिल्लो समय गरेका सांस्कृतिक पर्यटनका कार्यक्रमबारे विभागीय प्रमुखले जानकारी दिए। सांस्कृतिक संस्थानको आरम्भिक इतिहासदेखि जोडिएका राममान प्रधानसितको अन्तर्वार्ता र उनको ‘इतिहास बाँचिरहन्छ’ पुस्तक वास्तविकता जान्न अत्यन्त सहयोगी भएका छन्।
बाह्र वर्षमा मात्र नचाइने गथुप्याखंहरू धेरै लामो समय कुरेर अवलोकनपश्चात् लेख्न पाएकी छु।
नेवार समुदायका मुकुन्डोनाचबारे मूल रूपले सम्बन्धित नाचका गुरु, पात्र र नाचसित सम्बद्ध निकायसित अन्तर्वार्ता लिएर जानकारी हासिल गरिएको हो।
नेपालमा चर्यानर्तन पद्धतिलाई मात्र शास्त्रीय नृत्य मानिएको छ। यसको सैद्धान्तिक र प्रयोगात्मक पक्षबारे जे जति लेखिएको छ, त्यसको मूल स्रोत मेरा गुरुहरू आशाकाजी पण्डित, सप्तमुनि बज्राचार्य, रत्नकाजी बज्राचार्य, चैत्यराज बज्राचार्य, मोतीकाजी बज्राचार्य, यज्ञमानपति बज्राचार्य र फणीन्द्ररत्न बज्राचार्य हुन्। महिला गुर्जु र हेम बज्राचार्यले निकै सहयोग पुर्याए। यज्ञमान गुरुबाट चर्यासङ्गीत उल्लेख भएको तन्त्रबारे प्राप्त जानकारी अमूल्य रह्यो।
काठमाडौँको गथुप्याखंका पदस्थान, पदचालहरूको नाम र प्रत्येक देवदेवीले नाच्दा बनाउने मण्डलबारे रमेश मालाकारबाट धेरै जानकारी प्राप्त भएको थियो। यसैका आधारमा रेखाचित्र तयार गरिएको हो। केशव मालाकार, भरत मालाकार तथा राकेश मालीको पनि महत्त्वपूर्ण सहयोग पाएकी छु। वि.सं. २०३३ मा पहिलोपल्ट भद्रकालीनाच हेर्ने मौका पाउँदा तत्कालीन पुजारी देव मालीबाट पुराना कुराबारे जानकारी पाएकी थिएँ। भक्तपुरको गथुप्याखंबारे वि.सं. २०२७-०२८ मा नकी र नाय भएकाहरू र २०७५ सालमा सुरेश मालाकार, पूर्णकृष्ण चित्रकार, जुलाल कर्माचार्यबाट धेरै जानकारी प्राप्त भएका छन्।
कीर्तिपुरको गथुप्याखं र नाच बाहिर ल्याउन अनुमति दिने प्रधान गुठीका थकाली रुद्रबहादुर प्रधान, मुकुन्डोमा प्राणप्रतिष्ठा गर्ने धर्मराज बज्राचार्य, द्य:गुठीका थकाली अष्टमान डङ्गोलले पूजा पक्षबारे जानकारी दिए। अर्जुन माली, चन्द्रबहादुर माली र ‘किपूया गथुप्याखं’ पुस्तकका लेखक श्रीकृष्ण महर्जन धन्यवादका पात्र हुन्। थेचोको गथुप्याखंबारे जानकारी दिने राजेन्द्र माली, किरण माली, रामगोपाल माली, रमेश माली, रामबहादुर माली, धर्मराज माली र बाबुराजा माली सहयोगी रहे। वि.सं. २०४७-०४८ मा यस नाचमा भैरव भएर नाच्ने हेमराज माली र नन्दगोपाल, मुहाली बजाउने काइँला र साइँला कपालीबाट पनि धेरै जानकारी पाएँ। गुरुहरूको सहयोगमा नाच अवलोकन हुन नसकेको भए यो ग्रन्थ अधुरै रहने थियो। बाह्र वर्षमा मात्र नचाइने गथुप्याखंहरू धेरै लामो समय कुरेर अवलोकनपश्चात् लेख्न पाएकी छु।
ललितपुरको कार्तिकनाचबारे जानकारी दिने माणिकलाल चित्रकार, मङ्गलानन्द राजोपाध्याय, प्रमोद राजोपाध्याय, हरिमान श्रेष्ठ, केशव श्रेष्ठ, सिद्धिमान श्रेष्ठ, चक्रधर शर्मा, प्रतापधर शर्मा, सञ्जय शर्मा, तुलसीलाल सिंह, सुनिता राजभण्डारी प्रमुख हुन्। हरिमान श्रेष्ठको ‘कातिप्याखं’ र सुनिता राजभण्डारीको ‘कातीप्याखंनय् नृसिंह अवतार’ पुस्तकहरू निकै सहयोगी रहे। २०४७-०४८ सालमा फर्पिङको कार्तिकनाचबारे जानकारी दिने तत्कालीन जिम्मावाल गणेश मानन्धर प्रमुख हुन् भने रत्न बलामी, विष्णु बलामीबाट पनि धेरै जानकारी पाएकी छु। दक्षिणकाली नाचबारेको जानकारी प्रमुख पुजारी प्रकाश कर्माचार्यबाट पाएँ। वि.सं. २०४९ मा चित्लाङको कार्तिकनाच माझगाउँमा हेर्न जाँदा इन्द्रलाल बलामी, सिद्धिबहादुर बलामी, रामबहादुर बलामी, तत्कालीन भैरव गुठीका नाय र निर्मल बलामीबाट धेरै सूचना पाएँ। टिस्टुङको वज्रवाराहीनाचबारे जानकारी दिने पुजारी तीर्थराज कर्माचार्य र कवि जनकलाल गोपालीका सहयोग महत्त्वपूर्ण छन्। तेजप्रसाद श्रेष्ठले ‘नेपाली लोकवार्ता : विविध सन्दर्भ’ मा समेटेको ‘टिस्टुङको वज्रवाराहीनाच’ लाई मूल स्रोत नै माने हुन्छ।
किलागलको देवीनाचबारे वि.सं. २०२७-०२८ मा नाचका तत्कालीन गुरु ग्वारा महर्जन, उनका तीन छोरा एवं नाति राजु महर्जनसमेत तीन पुस्ताको सहयोगले इतिहाससँगै गुरु र पात्रको परम्पराबारे लेख्न सकिएको हो। ग्वारापछिका गुरु इन्द्र महर्जन र उनका छोरा नरेन्द्र महर्जनले लेखेको ‘देवीनाच : एक परिचय’ ले पनि ठूलो सहयोग पुर्याएको छ।
दाप्चा माथिल्लो हटियाको देवीभैरवनाचबारे वि.सं. २०७६ मा जानकारी दिने मुख्य गुरु रामकृष्ण श्रेष्ठ हुन्। ओमकृष्ण श्रेष्ठ, मणिरत्न श्रेष्ठ, गणेश श्रेष्ठ र रामकुमार श्रेष्ठले पनि धेरै सूचना दिए। दाप्चाकै तल्लो हटियाको देवीनाचबारे जानकारी दिएर साधुराम श्रेष्ठ, तेजकुमार श्रेष्ठ र प्रकाश श्रेष्ठले निकै ठूलो गुन लगाएका छन्।
लोप भइसकेको बनेपाली देवीनाचबारे बनेपावासी जानकारी मानन्धरले सुनेका आधारमा जानकारी दिए। पनौतीको देवीनाचबारे २०५४ सालमा गुरु हीरालाल प्रजापति र महादेव मानन्धरबाट जानकारी पाएँ। पछि बालकृष्ण प्रजापति र कृष्णजङ कर्माचार्यले सहयोग गरे। साँगाको देवीनाचबारे जानकारी दिने वि.सं. २०६२ का नाचगुरु गङ्गाबहादुर न्हुच्छे प्रमुख हुन्। हीराबहादुर माजुले पनि सूचना दिए। वि.सं. २०७४ मा अन्तर्वार्ता दिई पोगानाय रामकुमार खड्गी, विकास श्रेष्ठ, सुन्दरराज दुवाल, बोर्डर युथ क्लबका अध्यक्ष राजाराम दुवाल, सत्यनारायण डङ्गोल, सागर मानन्धर, अनुप जोशी र रामदास सखदेवले सहयोग गरे। साँखुको देवीनाचबारे वि.सं. २०४८ मै गुरु हीराकाजी स्यार्पाबाट जानकारी पाएकी थिएँ। २०७४ मा सुरेन्द्र गिरी, बलराम गिरी र हरिबोल श्रेष्ठबाट थप सूचना पाएँ। भोजपुर टक्सारको वनदेवीनाचबारेको जानकारी नाचगुरु नन्दलाल शाक्य, रेवतीकुमार ताम्राकार र दास शाक्यबाट पाएँ। पहिले ललितपुरको थैबमा प्रचलित रहे पनि हाल बन्द भइसकेको देवीनाचबारे भैरव भएर अन्तिमपल्ट नाच्ने मोहन श्रेष्ठ र आयोजक परिवारका मधुर न्ववँ (श्रेष्ठ) ले जानकारी दिए। भक्तपुरको महाकालीनाचबारे वि.सं. २०२७-०२८ मा जानकारी दिने प्रमुख जननीदास दैवज्ञ हुन्। पछि उपेन्द्र दैवज्ञ, कोमलानन्द जोशी, खर्बुजा समूहबाट रामचन्द्र खर्बुजा, हरिभक्त फैँजु, बुलाल हलेजु, लक्ष्मीप्रसाद माकजु, लोहना समूहबाट रामप्रसाद लोहना, बाबुराज दण्डेख्वा, तुलसी दण्डेख्वाबाट धेरै जानकारी पाएँ। पछिल्लो विस्तारबारे जानकारी दिने मुक्तिसुन्दर जधारी हुन्। मुस्याख्वा समूहबाट दिलबहादुर श्रेष्ठ, शिवलाल मुस्याख्वा, रामगोपाल सुलजु, नाति शुद्धिकार, कृष्णभक्त मानन्धर र हरिभक्त फैँजुले जानकारी दिएका थिए। थिमिको महाकालीनाचबारे नगदेशका महाकाली नाचगुरु भक्तबहादुर ध्वजु, श्रीगोपाल प्रजापति, विनोद कोजु र गणेश लाछिले जानकारी दिए। बोद्यको नीलवाराहीनाचबारे सञ्जीव था: श्रेष्ठले जानकारी दिएका हुन्।
नेवार समुदायका परम्परागत मुकुन्डोनाचबारे प्रकाशित पुस्तक र लेखहरूले मलाई धेरै सहयोग पुग्यो।
भैरवनाचमा संलग्न भक्तपुरको भैलप्याखंका तीन समूहबारेको जानकारी कृष्ण प्रजापति, हरिशरण अवाले, रामकुमार अवाले, मोहनकुमार हाकुचाखल, तुलसीभगत र विष्णुभगतबाट पाएँ। थिमिको भैलप्याखंबारे भने श्रीगोपाल प्रजापति, गणेश लाछि, थिमि लाय्कु नाय श्यामकाजी श्रेष्ठ, नाचका संयोजक तथा नाचगुरु अर्जुन श्रेष्ठ, बाजागुरु निरज श्रेष्ठ हुन्। फुँसीखेलको मनमय्जु जात्राबारे रामकाजी राजबाहकले जानकारी दिए। त्यसै गरी पोखराको भैरवनाचबारे २०२८ सालमा सर्वज्ञमान प्रधानाङ्ग, त्यसपछि केशवदास प्रधानाङ्ग, तीर्थ श्रेष्ठ, कृष्णमान प्रधानाङ्ग, कृष्ण श्रेष्ठ, रमेश श्रेष्ठ र जितेन्द्र बाताजुले जानकारी दिए। अर्घाखाँचीको भैरवनाचबारेको जानकारी र फोटो श्रीनारायण श्रेष्ठबाट प्राप्त भएको हो। अहिले लोप भइसकेको हाँडीगाउँको विष्णुदेवी मुकुन्डोनाचबारे सूर्यलाल प्रजापतिबाट जानकारी पाएँ।
श्वेतकालीनाचबारे २०२७-०२८ सालमै सप्तमुनि वज्राचार्य, ताःगुरु ज्योतिरत्न तुलाधर, तत्कालीन धामी देवकृष्ण महर्जनबाट जानकारी पाएकी थिएँ। पछि तानाय् राजप्रसाद तुलाधर, मचानानी महर्जनबाट थप जानकारी पाएँ। डा. राजेन्द्र प्रधानले श्वेतकालीनाचको बाह्र वर्षको पूजाबारे जानकारी दिएको हो।
जलप्याखंबारे रमानन्दप्रसाद सिंह, लिटिल लिन्डा (अमेरिकी नागरिक), सकलबहादुर महर्जन, धनबहादुर च्याभू, राम च्याभू र राम महर्जनले धेरै कुरा बताए। सिकालीप्याखंबारे मूल जानकारी शान्त महर्जनबाट पाएँ। आकाशभैरवनाचबारे मन्दिरका पुजारी नरे पुतवारबाट जानकारी लिएँ। मजिपाः लाखय्बारे जानकारी दिनेमा विनोद रञ्जितकार, लक्ष्मण तथा यमुना रञ्जितकार प्रमुख छन्।
ललितपुरको लाखय् नाचबारे उत्तम शाक्य, भोजपुरको लाखय् नाचबारे रामेश्वर तमोट र राजु सिकर्मीबाट जानकारी लिएँ। भक्तपुरको माकःप्याखंबारे सो नाचका गुरु भारचोका हरिभक्त कोजु, गणेशभक्त कोजु र काजीनारायण सिंताखल प्रमुख सूचक हुन्। बाग्लुङको हनुमाननाचबारे प्रेम छोटा, सुवास श्रेष्ठ; बेनीबजारको हनुमान्नाचबारे सुन्दर शाक्य, सुदर्शनकुमार श्रेष्ठ, बुटवलका राधेश्याम राजभण्डारी र कुस्माका इन्द्रकुमार विकल्पहरूबाट धेरै जानकारी लिएँ।
नेवार समुदायका परम्परागत मुकुन्डोनाचबारे प्रकाशित पुस्तक र लेखहरूले मलाई धेरै सहयोग पुग्यो। नाच र तिनको ऐतिहासिक पक्ष जोडिएका चाडपर्व र जात्राबारेका पुस्तक पनि सहयोगी भए। संस्कृतिविद् सत्यमोहन जोशी, साफल्य अमात्य, हरिराम जोशी, रत्नकाजी वज्राचार्य, फणीन्द्र बज्राचार्य, विनोद राजभण्डारी, भुवनलाल प्रधान, श्रीगोपाल प्रजापति, पुरुषोत्तमलोचन श्रेष्ठ, प्रेम छोटा, वासुपासा, सकलबहादुर महर्जन, नरेन्द्र महर्जन, राजेन्द्र तुबंजा श्रेष्ठ, हरिराम जोशी, तेजप्रकाश श्रेष्ठ, प्रदीप जामन, डा. तुलसीनारायण श्रेष्ठ, राममान प्रधान, शान्त नेवा, बालगोपाल श्रेष्ठ, श्रीकृष्ण महर्जन, हेमराज शाक्य, सन सायमि, यज्ञमान वज्राचार्य, धर्मरत्न शाक्य, ध्रुव मानन्धर, डा. चुन्दा वज्राचार्य, सुनिता राजभण्डारी, प्रेमबहादुर कसा, चित्तधर हृदय, प्रचण्ड मल्ल, करुणाकर वैद्य, मुक्तिसुन्दर जधारी, नानीहीरा शाक्य, रामबहादुर रावत आदिका पुस्तक र लेखहरू जानकारीका स्रोत हुन्।
पुस्तकमा समेटिएका अधिकांश मुकुन्डोनाच अवलोकन गरी तिनको प्रविधि र प्रस्तुति लेखिएको हो। प्रदर्शनकारी कला भएकाले नृत्यको प्रविधि र प्रस्तुति बुझ्न फोटोको भूमिका गहन हुन्छ। २०२६ देखि २०८२ सालसम्मको यस यात्रामा विभिन्न पेसाका व्यक्तित्वको सहयोग प्राप्त भएको छ। डा. आनन्द प्रधान, डा. राजेन्द्र प्रधान, रोजर (अमेरिकी नागरिक), मुकुन्द श्रेष्ठ, कीर्तनमङ्गल जोशी, प्रकाश श्रेष्ठ, विमलचन्द्र शर्मा नेपाली, कृष्णकुमारी महर्जन, दीपक लामिछाने, गोविन्द महर्जन, प्रशान्त श्रेष्ठ, सुदर्शन शाक्य (मूर्तिकार), विज्ञान श्रेष्ठ (पोस्टर बनाउने) प्रमुख हुन्। नाम थाहा नभएका केही विदेशी फोटोग्राफरहरूबाट पनि सहयोग पाएकी छु। विमलचन्द्र शर्माले प्रायः सबै तस्बिर खोज्न र मिलाउन सहयोग गरेर मलाई चिन्तामुक्त गराए। आकर्षक फोटो डिजाइनमा बहिनी प्रेरिता शर्माले लिएको जिम्मेवारीप्रति नतमस्तक छु। डा. आनन्द र डा. राजेन्द्रले खिचेका फोटा केही गुरुहरूसित लिएका अन्तर्वार्ताका प्रमाण पनि भएका छन्। नाति आलोक जोशीले भद्रकालीनाचको प्रस्तुति रेखाचित्रमा उतारेको हो।
चर्यानृत्य गुरुहरूले नृत्य गरिरहेका तस्बिर अमूल्य छन्। यस पुस्तकमा राखिएका फोटोका सबै फोटोग्राफरहरूमा हार्दिक आभार व्यक्त गर्दै कसैको नाम छुटेमा क्षमा चाहन्छु। नासःद्यःको सर्वेक्षण गरी सङ्कलन गरिएका तस्बिर दिने डा. फ्रेक बेन्डलप्रति आभारी छु। सबै तस्बिर म आफैँले सङ्कलन गर्न सम्भव थिएन। खास गरी जात्राका धेरै तस्बिर नाति कीर्तनमङ्गल जोशीले जुटाइदिए।
पुस्तकको भाषा नेपाली भए पनि नाचसित जोडिएका धेरै शब्दहरू नेवार चलनचल्तीका शब्दमै राख्नु जरुरी थियो।
परम्परागत मुकुन्डोनाच मनोरञ्जनका लागि मात्र नभएर समूह, जातजाति, आदिवासीको पहिचान, धार्मिक मान्यता, सांस्कृतिक र सामाजिक परम्परालाई जीवन्त राख्दै आएको प्रदर्शनकारी कला हो। यसलाई विस्तार गर्दै नाच जोगाइराख्ने र ऐतिहासिक पक्ष अझ खोज्ने जिम्मेवारी युवा पुस्तामा छाडेकी छु। नेवार समुदायले मान्दै आएका धर्म, संस्कृति, सामाजिक रीतिरिवाज आदि कुनै पनि क्षेत्रको खोज आरम्भ गर्न सकिन्छ तर अन्त हुँदैन। नेवार मात्र होइन, नेपालका सबै समुदाय, जातजाति, आदिवासीले परम्परागत नृत्यको इतिहास खोजी गरी आफ्नो पहिचान जोगाउनतिर उन्मुख हुने आशा गर्दछु।
‘नृत्य विषय लिएर विश्वविद्यालयसम्म पुग्ने तिमीले यसबारे पुस्तक नलेखे कसले लेख्ने ?’ आदरणीय संस्कृतिविद् सत्यमोहन जोशीले बोलेको त्यो आवाज मेरो कानमा अझै गुन्जिरहेछ। दुर्भाग्य ! उहाँको जीवन छँदै त्यो इच्छा पूरा गर्न सकिनँ। संस्कृतिविद् हरिराम जोशीले पुस्तक प्रकाशन गर्न प्रेरित गरिरहनुभयो। यसैगरी संस्कृतिविद् तुलसी दिवसले पनि हरेक पटक भेट हुँदा ‘किताब कहिले आउँछ ?’ भनेर सोधिरहनुभयो। संस्कृति क्षेत्रका यी सबै हस्तीहरूलाई नमन गर्छु।
लेखन, भाषिक प्रस्तुति र साहित्य आफैँमा श्रेष्ठ कला हो तर यसबारे पूर्ण जानकारी नहुनु मेरो कमजोर पक्ष हो। यस पक्षमा खण्डखण्ड मात्र भए पनि पहिलो व्याकरणगत शुद्धीकरण गर्न मद्दत गर्ने महानुभाव सर्वप्रथम हर्षनाथ भट्टराईलाई सम्मान गर्न चाहन्छु। उहाँपछि, क्षेत्रबहादुर कायस्थ, दिपना शर्मा, विमल शर्मा, पुरुषोत्तम ढकाल, प्रदिपा श्रेष्ठ, ध्रुव मधिकर्मी र ईश्वरमान सिन्याहरूप्रति कृतज्ञ छु।
पछि आएर विशेष समय छुट्याई पाण्डुलिपि तयारी र भाषिक शुद्धीकरणमा कमल सुवेदी खट्नुभयो। भाषिक शुद्धीकरणमै जोडिएका वेदराज ढुङ्गानालगायत धेरै महानुभावहरू धन्यवादका पात्र हुनुहुन्छ।
पुस्तकको भाषा नेपाली भए पनि नाचसित जोडिएका धेरै शब्दहरू नेवार चलनचल्तीका शब्दमै राख्नु जरुरी थियो। केही नाचमा ठाउँ अनुसार एउटै कुराका लागि प्रयोग गरिने शब्द फरक फरक पनि पाइयो। नेपालीकरण गरिएका केही नाम नेवार भाषामा लेख्दा फरक हुँदो रहेछ। म मधेसकी नेवार, साधारण नेवार भाषा बोल्न र बुझ्न त सक्छु तर स्तरीकृत नेवार भाषा मेरो वशको कुरा रहेन। यो समस्या समाधानको सिङ्गो जिम्मेवारी लिने कार्तिकनाचकी शोधार्थी एवं नेपाल भाषाकी प्राध्यापक सुनिता राजभण्डारीको पूर्ण सहयोगप्रति आभारी छु।
म ‘कम्प्युटर लिटरेट’ हुन सकिनँ। त्यसैले सुरुदेखि किरण श्रेष्ठ र मीन महर्जनले निकै सहयोग गर्नुभयो। तर, धेरै वर्षपछि पुनः लेख्न थालेपछि सुन्दा शाक्य, सुनिल शाक्य, उर्गेन डङ्गोल, अनिता डङ्गोल अक्षर विन्यासमा निरन्तर खट्नुभयो। यथार्थमा सुन्दा शाक्य र कमल सुवेदी पुस्तकका निमित्त सबैभन्दा नजिकका आफन्त बन्नुभयो। पुस्तक अन्तिम तयारीको क्रममा समग्र पाण्डुलिपि सम्पादन, पृष्ठविन्यास, भाषिक-व्याकरणगत शुद्धीकरण र स्रोत विश्लेषणमा होम भट्टराईको मेहनत उदाहरणीय छ।
विगतको कोरोना महामारीका बेला कोही न कोही मरेको सुनेर होला, त्यतिखेर सात वर्ष मात्र भएको नाति आयान जोशीले “मा ! चाँडै किताब छापिहाल्नुस्, तपाईं मरिहाल्यो भने तपाईंले लेखेको सबै डस्टबिनमा जान्छ” भनेका शब्दले सधैँ घचघच्याइरहे पनि पाँच-छ वर्ष बितेपछि मात्र प्रकाशन गर्न भ्याइयो। तर जे होस्, मेरो नातिका ती शब्दले मलाई पुनः प्रेरित गरेका हुन्। नातिनी मेधावी श्रेष्ठले पनि विभिन्न अभिलेखहरूको फोटोकपी गर्न सहयोग गरेकी छिन्। पुस्तक प्रकाशनमा ल्याउन अमेरिकादेखि फोन गरेर घचघच्याउने बालसखा मञ्जु हाडाप्रति म ऋणी छु। त्यसै गरी मुद्रणको प्रबन्ध मिलाउने कृष्ण के.सी. तथा आकर्षक आवरण डिजाइनसहित मुद्रणमा निरन्तर खट्ने रवि महर्जन एवं सार्थक प्रिन्टिङ एन्ड अफिस सप्लाइका सबै भाइबहिनी धन्यवादका उदाहरणीय पात्र हुन्।
अन्तमा, १०० वर्ष पुगिसकेकी मेरी आमा गङ्गादेवी राजभण्डारी, जसले बुबा बितेकै वर्ष आफन्तहरूले रोक्दारोक्दै पनि मलाई विश्वास गरेर नृत्य अध्ययन गर्न अनुमति दिनुभयो। मेरो जीवन उहाँको ऋणमा डुबेको छ, जसलाई म चुकाउन चाहन्नँ।
२०८२, माघ

title: Women’s struggles, social movements brought together in new book
content:
Culture & Lifestyle
Women’s struggles, social movements brought together in new book
‘Shared Dreams Woven by Struggle’ documents the journeys of 13 women leaders who fought for rights, dignity and social justice.Post Report
The journeys and struggles of 13 women leaders who have contributed to Nepal’s social movements have been brought together in a new research book, ‘Shared Dreams Woven by Struggle’, launched in Lalitpur on Friday.
The book, published by Voices of Women Media, documents the lives, struggles, and contributions of women who challenged discrimination, organised communities, and fought for rights, dignity, and social justice. Through their personal stories, it traces some of the social movements that have shaped Nepali society while drawing attention to the often-overlooked role of women in those struggles.
For instance, the book includes the story of Uma Devi Badi and her struggle for land, rights, and dignity as part of the Badi community’s rights movement. It also documents the journey of Muskan Khatun, who survived an acid attack and has continued her struggle for justice and dignity.
Some of the stories revisit the Sino Bahishkar Movement, which has gradually faded from public memory. The experiences of Mahari Devi, Bhola Devi and Chandeshwori Sada, who were involved in the movement, offer a glimpse into the courage of women who challenged caste-based discrimination and fought for equality and dignity.
Speaking at the launch, chief guest Sunita Dangol, acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City, said documenting such histories was itself an important part of the struggle for women’s rights.
“We need to remember that until it is written, it won’t be written. Writing and documenting these experiences is a strong way to establish our own narrative in a society where women’s struggles and voices are questioned time and again,” she said.
Following the launch, a panel discussion titled ‘Women Leaders and Social Movements: Reflections and Practices’ brought together activists, academicians, researchers and representatives from different fields to reflect on women’s leadership and the continuing relevance of social movements.
The discussion was moderated by Hemlata Rai, a Women, Peace and Security expert. Panellists included Muna Shakya, disability rights advocate; Parbati BK, Member of the Federal Parliament of Nepal; Rita Baramu, writer, researcher and digital rights activist; and Jamuna Siwakoti, head of the Central Department of Gender Studies at Tribhuvan University.

title: Wonder Rooster, historic Mango tree put Lundo Island’s cultural heritage under tourism spotlight again
content:
Wonder Rooster, historic Mango tree put Lundo Island’s cultural heritage under tourism spotlight again
AT the shores of Lake Nyasa, beneath an old mango tree closely associated with the history of Lundo Island, domestic tourists recently encountered something more enduring than scenery: a living account of culture, tradition and memory. Gathered around the tree, they listened to island elder Vincent Tadei, popularly known as Mzee Magogo, as he recounted stories and beliefs that have helped shape Lundo’s cultural identity across generations.
The encounter offered visitors an opportunity to understand Lundo beyond its waters and natural beauty. It presented the island as a place where history survives through people, places and oral traditions. At the centre of the experience was the old mango tree, whose history, according to accounts shared with visitors, is linked to lepers who lived on or visited the island in earlier times. It was beneath and around this historic tree, close to the lakeshore, that the visitors participated in a traditional moment of prayer.
Mzee Magogo explained that, according to local tradition and belief, visitors to Lundo may make prayers through traditional practices by directing their requests towards the island’s famous “Wonder Rooster.” The rooster is among the most intriguing stories associated with Lundo. For years, local people have regarded it as a distinctive part of the island’s traditional heritage. Its exact age is unknown and even those responsible for managing the island do not know precisely how long it has lived there.
According to Mzee Magogo, the rooster remains within the island’s reserve and appears to visitors according to patterns that are not readily understood. Some people arrive hoping to see it and leave without doing so, while others encounter it during their visit. That uncertainty has become part of the story surrounding the bird and contributes to the curiosity it generates among visitors.
For the domestic tourists who travelled from Mbamba Bay to Lundo Island through an initiative organised by Jogoo FM Radio, the encounter was particularly memorable. They became the second known group of tourists in 2026 to see the Wonder Rooster, according to information shared by people familiar with visits to the island.
A group of Namtumbo District Council employees who recently visited Lundo was also reported to have seen the bird, while many other visitors during 2026 had not. Across Tanzania, generations have passed knowledge through elders, stories, sacred places, songs, dances, ceremonies and traditional practices. Lundo is one of the places where elements of that inheritance remain part of community identity.
Mzee Magogo therefore serves a role extending beyond that of a guide. As an elder familiar with local traditions, he provides a link between the island’s past and present. Lundo’s history cannot be understood only through its lake, mountains, birds or wildlife. It is also contained in memories associated with people and places. The old mango tree illustrates this point. For those familiar with its history, it is more than vegetation; it is a physical reference to an earlier period in the island’s life and to experiences that shaped how the place is remembered.
This form of heritage gives cultural tourism a deeper purpose. A visitor who comes only to admire the lake may leave with photographs, while one who listens to local stories may leave with a stronger understanding of the community’s identity and relationship with its surroundings. Domestic tourism can therefore create opportunities for Tanzanians to discover histories and traditions within their own country that might otherwise remain unfamiliar.
The experience also raises questions about preservation. What happens when elders who carry such knowledge are no longer available to tell it? Cultural heritage can disappear gradually when stories stop being transmitted, historic places lose their meaning or younger generations grow up without understanding why certain traditions matter.
Preserving heritage does not mean accepting every traditional belief without question. It means documenting, understanding and respecting cultural knowledge while ensuring that traditions are presented responsibly and that practices remain consistent with safety, human dignity and conservation.
This approach allows communities to retain their heritage while engaging with changing social realities. People such as Mzee Magogo are important to that process because their knowledge may contain histories unavailable elsewhere.
Local authorities, tourism institutions, researchers, schools and communities can collaborate to document oral histories, traditional stories, significant sites and cultural practices associated with Lundo Island. Young Tanzanians can also participate by interviewing elders, recording stories, studying local history and sharing cultural knowledge responsibly with visitors. Such efforts can turn heritage into a living inheritance rather than something remembered only after it has disappeared.
The visitors from Mbamba Bay did not merely reach an island; they encountered an elder, listened to traditions and experienced a cultural narrative rooted in the place. Such encounters can broaden the meaning of domestic tourism by encouraging curiosity, respect and learning. Lundo Island consequently offers more than scenery. The Wonder Rooster, the old mango tree and Mzee Magogo’s stories form different elements of a wider cultural narrative. For visitors, they can inspire curiosity; for the local community, they represent heritage; and for younger generations, they provide lessons about preserving history.
As domestic tourism expands, destinations such as Lundo have an opportunity to place culture alongside natural attractions. The lake may draw visitors and the island’s landscape may encourage exploration, but stories can give the destination a deeper identity. The gathering beneath the old mango tree was therefore more than a moment of prayer.
It was an encounter between the present and the past and an opportunity to hear a cultural history that cannot be measured only through visitor numbers or economic value. Lundo’s enduring lesson is that heritage exists not only in monuments and historical objects, but also in stories, memories, elders and places. Preserving those elements requires documentation, responsible tourism and intergenerational learning.
For the island, preserving these accounts can strengthen cultural pride while helping visitors appreciate heritage beyond the landscape itself. For the visitors beside Lake Nyasa, the journey became an encounter with memory and tradition. In that sense, one of Lundo’s greatest treasures is a story still being told.

title: Namen zu Gastarbeiter-Bildern gesucht
content:
Sie kamen als Gastarbeiter und blieben als Nachbarn: Vor 60 Jahren begann das Anwerbeabkommen mit Jugoslawien, das Menschen auf Arbeitssuche einen Job in Vorarlberg ermöglichte. Viele der Porträtierten sind bis heute unerkannt. Das soll sich nun ändern.
„Kultur am Bahnhof“ mit buntem Programm
Die Aktion „Kultur am Bahnhof“ bringt vier Mal jährlich Farbe dorthin, wo ansonsten umgestiegen oder Halt gemacht wird. Diesmal reichte das Programm von Zirkuseinlagen über Livemusik bis hin zum Museumsmobil – wo Fotos von Gastarbeitern aus dem ehemaligen Jugoslawien gezeigt wurden.
Alten Bildern Namen und Geschichten zuordnen
Das Ziel war, sich auszutauschen und vielleicht Personen auf den Fotos zu wiederzuerkennen, erklärte Historikerin Barbara Motter vom Stadtmuseum Dornbirn gegenüber dem ORF Vorarlberg: „Wir wissen einfach nur, dass diese Fotos in Dornbirn entstanden, bei der Firma Hämmerle oder auch bei der Firma Getzner Bludenz. Und wir möchten mit der kleinen Ausstellung eine Art Aufruf machen: Wer hilft uns beim Identifizieren?“
Aber nicht nur Namen sind gefragt, sagt Motter: „Natürlich interessiert uns auch die Geschichte dazu. Wie ist man angekommen? Wo hat man gewohnt am Anfang? Wie waren die ersten Jahre in Dornbirn?“
Das „Büro für Arbajteri“
Sechs Prozent der Bevölkerung – also rund 25.000 Menschen – in Vorarlberg haben einen Familienbezug zum ehemaligen Jugoslawien. Auch Renate Fussenegger – sie kam mit 18 Jahren nach Österreich, um zu arbeiten. Ihre Geschichte erzählte sie am Museumsmobil: „Ich kam mit dem Bus, das hat alles F.M. Rhomberg organisiert. So kam ich 1968 nach Dornbirn und seither bin ich hier, habe 40 Jahre gearbeitet und eine glückliche Familie gegründet.“
„Kultur am Bahnhof“
nächster Termin am Freitag, 9. Oktober 2026 zwischen 12.00 und 17.00 Uhr am Bahnhof Dornbirn.
Am Anfang im Tierheim Zimmer gemietet
Auch der 96-jährige Wilfried Klocker aus Dornbirn erzählte von früher. Er wurde von seiner ehemaligen Firma beauftragt, Arbeitskräfte im ehemaligen Jugoslawien zu suchen: „Aber das Problem war immer die Unterkunft. Am Anfang haben wir sie sogar im Tierheim Hatlerdorf untergebracht, da hatten wir zwei oder drei Zimmer für ein paar Leute gemietet. Aber irgendwie hat man’s gerichtet.“
Mehrere Menschen konnten an diesem Tag auf den Fotos identifiziert werden.

title: Aboriginal man's fight for justice after alleged historical abuse at hospital
content:
Uncle Benjamin 'BJ' Cruse's fight for justice after alleged historical healthcare abuse
Uncle Benjamin 'BJ' Cruse says he has lived with a lifetime of trauma stemming from a few days in hospital.
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this article contains the names and images of an Indigenous person who has died, used with the permission of family.
Warning: This story contains details that may be distressing for some readers.
As a young boy, he was treated for dysentery, an intestinal infection which causes severe diarrhoea, with his siblings at Macleay District Hospital on the New South Wales Mid North Coast.
The Yuin and Monaroo elder remembers being placed on a verandah with his brother and sister at the health facility now known as Kempsey District Hospital, and the rooms being partitioned with "hessian bag material".
"That's where Aboriginal people were kept," he said.
It was here Mr Cruse alleges he was physically and emotionally abused, including being slapped multiple times on the face by a nurse.
He said he was told to kneel on the bed with his back straight, as books were stacked on his head.
"When the nurse heard the books fall on the floor … she yanked me off the bed and slapped me on both sides of the face,"he said.
The now 72-year-old also claimed being given apron strings to hold in each hand and forced to follow the nurse around the ward as she treated other patients.
"If she walked too fast, I'd pull both apron strings undone and she'd turn around and slap me on both sides of the face," he said.
The almost-week long ordeal left Mr Cruse with psychological issues, he said.
His sister, Aunty Rhonda Cruse-Rawiri, recalled being kept in a dark, separate room away from other patients.
"I could see out of that room where they had all the non-Aboriginal kids and it was really bright in there, all the toys and a big rocking horse," she said.
"I remember standing at the door waiting to go out and the nurse came … shooing us back in the room.
"And the [hospital] gown we had [on] had A-B-O across the back."
Their father, Uncle Ossie Cruse, who is now in his early 90s, also remembered the gowns from when he picked his children up from the hospital.
"And I thought, 'Wow, we're out of here'," he told Australian Story in 2017.
"I just grabbed the kids, and we never even went to see the people. We just took them out and went home."
'An insult'
Now, Mr Cruse is calling for an apology and "proper and just" compensation for his alleged abuse, taking his demands to the state government, as well as the United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues.
But he said on multiple occasions the government referred him to existing schemes, including the NSW Stolen Generations Reparation Scheme, and the National Redress Scheme created following the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse schemes, both of which he is not eligible for.
"This is something that has gone under the radar, it's fallen through the cracks and just because it [the alleged abuse] doesn't meet that criteria," Mr Cruse said.
"I believe it shouldn't give the government the option to opt out of their responsibility."
However, since engaging lawyers, Mr Cruse said the local health district had now offered him compensation.
Though for him, he said it was not enough to make it right.
"I would receive a payment of $30,000 in the hand and to me that is an insult," he said.
"The government is holding me at ransom … knowing I can't fight the matter in court and that's why I wanted to bring the matter to the nation."
A Mid North Coast Local Health District spokesperson said in a statement it "does not comment on matters that are the subject of legal proceedings".
"The NSW government acknowledges and remembers the survivors of historical abuse and the past failures of governments and institutions to protect them," they said.
"The NSW government remains committed to ensuring survivors of historical abuse receive appropriate support and justice."
It also said all government agencies dealing with civil claims of child abuse followed guiding principles to make "litigation a less traumatic experience for victims".
'Deemed the right thing to do'
Mr Cruse said he and his siblings were taken to the Macleay District Hospital when he was about five years old, making it the late 1950s or early 1960s.
According to the Macleay River Historical Society, segregation ended at the hospital in July 1964.
Former nurse, scholar and labour historian, Odette Best, said this was "a very thick and murky era" for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander staff and patients.
"It was deemed the right thing to do that Indigenous people were not allowed to be nursed in the same ward as non-Indigenous people," Dr Best, a Gorreng Gorreng, Boonthamurra and Yugambeh woman said.
"The contested care that has actually been inflicted upon Aboriginal people has been full of abuse and neglect … [and] has left very deep ongoing scars for many, many Indigenous people."
Dr Best acknowledged while many nurses "do absolutely amazing work and do care for our communities", there were historical aspects that needed to be reconciled.
"Nursing has really got this huge history of this contested care that has really never been spoken about, talked about or addressed as a profession … that we actually participated in some pretty horrendous acts against Indigenous people,"she said.
National Justice Project CEO George Newhouse said there were still remnants of past policies within the healthcare system.
"People can die as a result of a doctor, or a nurse, or a clinician having a closed mind," he said.
"So even today we see hangovers of the segregation in the past and the low standard of healthcare provided to First Nations people."
Fear of being taken
As a child, Mr Cruse and his family moved around as his father Uncle Ossie Cruse followed the fruit and vegetable picking seasons as a seasonal worker, which led them to stay near Kempsey.
"For those 11 years up until 1967, we lived in tents, on the riverbanks, or on the beaches … and dad fished off the beach with nets or worked in the timber industry as a sleeper cutter," Mr Cruse said.
"So, we were what they called itinerant workers, living on the fringe camps."
The family eventually moved to Sydney where Mr Cruse and Ms Cruse-Rawiri remembered the NSW Aborigines Welfare Board visited their home.
Up until the late 1960s, the welfare board previously named the Aborigines Protection Board, controlled the lives and affairs of Aboriginal people in NSW by enforcing policies of segregation, assimilation, child removal and wage withholding.
"They went through the house, checked all our sheets, checked the cupboards, checked everything," Ms Cruse-Rawiri said.
"When my dad came home that afternoon he [went] into the room, and we had these little brown suitcases, and dad came back out to us and said whatever you can fit into those little bags you put it in cause we are leaving.
"My nan used to say if you see a car coming … you run as fast as you can and you hide.
"We were never stolen, but we grew up with the fear of being taken."
Ever since, Mr Cruse has been an advocate for his community and was involved in the land rights movement for decades.
His latest fight is his most personal: he is hoping to continue advocating for those who may have fallen through the cracks, like him.
"It's something that needs to be picked up and addressed because [there's been] much suffering for [our] people and their descendants … and it's still outstanding today," he said.
"I believe this will go a long way to healing."

title: Holy Trinity Oak Tree Chapel in Čibukovac, Serbia
content: The Holy Trinity oak chapel in Čibukovac, a small village near Kraljevo, is built inside a pedunculate oak believed to be over 500 years old. It is thought to be the oldest oak in Serbia. The tree stands more than 30 metres tall, with a trunk circumference of about 8 metres and a diameter of roughly two and a half metres, wide enough that villager Mihailo Erotijević, with the help of Father Radojko and others, was able to hollow out its trunk and turn it into a small working chapel. Since the feast of the Holy Trinity is the village's main Slava (a custom in the Serbian Orthodox tradition), the chapel took that dedication naturally. The interior was coated with wax to help preserve it, and small niches hold icons of the Holy Trinity, the Theotokos (Mother of God), the Great Martyr George the Victorious, St. Basil of Ostrog, the Crucifixion, and St. Paraskeva (Petka), a saint especially beloved across the Balkans. Villagers still gather there for major feast days in the Serbian Orthodox Calendar, and some visit alone simply to pray. There is also a local detail that adds to its mystery and why it is special. Before the tree became a chapel, it was frequently struck by lightning, something residents see as part of its passage from an ordinary ancient oak into a site of devotion. The Holy Trinity Oak Tree Chapel a striking, living echo of zapis meaning "inscription", an old Slavic traditions of venerating sacred trees across Serbian villages.

title: Richmond Night Market prepares for its grand finale
content:
When the Richmond Night Market’s neon lights turn off for the last time on Sunday, the Metro Vancouver community will say goodbye to one of the region’s most vibrant cultural gatherings after 26 years.
The event, which ran on weekends from April to September, was founded by entrepreneur Raymond Cheung in 2000 to bring public night-time culture inspired by Asian night markets to the B.C. suburb.
Mr. Cheung announced the market’s permanent closing last month. He said the market’s lease near Bridgeport station was ending, and that the potential cost of taking on a new, pricier lease wouldn’t make sense for the business.
The market originally opened at Continental Shopping Centre in Richmond. Over the years, it moved to bigger sites, evolving into what organizers claim is North America’s largest night market. It drew more than one million visitors, tourists and locals alike, each year. The market hosted upwards of 200 vendors selling food, clothing and more in brightly lit stalls.
Since relocating in 2012 to its current location near Bridgeport station, the market became a major cultural and economic anchor in the region.
With its lease expiring and no affordable new site to welcome the large event, the only course of action seemed to be to close the market. “It’s a very mixed feeling,” owner Mr. Cheung said.
“The sad part, of course, is this is the end of the chapter. I didn’t expect this to last forever,” he said. “… But this market is about bonding, it’s about community – that’s what it is.”
For families like the Purbas, who drove from nearby Delta for their fourth visit this season, the closure cuts deep. “We’re sad that it is closing, but it is the last weekend we can attend, so that’s why we’re here,” Gagandeep Purba said.
The market’s reputation is known across borders. Jesica Vinson travelled from Seattle with her family to catch the final season. “Is there any way to save it?” she asked.
Behind the food stalls, however, many long-term vendors were feeling at peace. At Po Wah Dim Sum, Christopher Yee helped his mother, Lai Wah, wrap up a legacy of more than two decades running the family business. “My mom has been doing it for 26 years and she’s retiring this year,” Mr. Yee said.
Others, such as Francis Dela Chica of Bao Buns, have accepted the closing as bittersweet. He said that while it’s sad that the night market is ending, it was also the perfect incubator for small businesses like his own. “It was a good place to start, to test your products, to meet new customers.”

title: Ogun community seeks support on tourism
content:
Traditional leaders of Ebute-Igbooro in Yewa North Local Government Area of Ogun State have called on the state government to provide infrastructure and other facilities to transform Oleyo Waterfall into a major cultural and tourist attraction.
They said the ancient waterfall had existed for generations and historically played an important role in the cultural and spiritual life of the people.
The Elebute of Ebute-Igbooro, Alhaji Amusa Dosumu, in statement made available to our correspondent on Saturday, said the waterfall was situated on Ebute-Igbooro land and belonged to the community.
Oba Dosumu spoke about the cultural significance of the Oleyo Waterfall, saying the community had continued to associate the spring with positive experiences and good water.
“There are many benefits because this Oleyo water does not tolerate evil. We see that it brings good water,” he said.
The traditional ruler appealed to the Ogun State Government to support the community in developing and promoting the site, particularly as part of efforts to preserve Yoruba cultural heritage and attract visitors.
Similarly, the Balogun of Ebute-Igbooro, Jeremiah Ijiola, described Oleyo as a remarkable natural and cultural heritage whose potential, he said, had not been fully explored.
Ijiola said members of the community had traditionally visited the location to pray, adding that the spring had been associated with local traditional practices for generations.
“Nobody ever thought that something as wonderful and awe-inspiring as this existed here,” he said.
He explained that prayers and traditional activities had historically been conducted at the location, adding that the community had stories of rainfall occurring during such occasions.
Ijiola urged the government to take ownership of the development process by providing infrastructure and facilities that could make Oleyo Waterfall accessible to tourists and visitors.
He drew a comparison with the development of Olumo Rock in Abeokuta, saying Oleyo Waterfall could similarly be transformed into a destination capable of attracting visitors from within and outside the country.
“Just like they took care of Olumo, how they renovated Olumo Rock so that it became a tourist centre—where people come from far away distances,” he said.
The Youth Leader of Ebute-Igbooro, Emmanuel Akan, also said the waterfall was not a recent discovery, explaining that the existence and traditional significance of the spring had been passed down through generations.
“Oleyo has been here long before we were born. Long before our fathers gave birth to us, we heard that Oleyo was here and that they used to worship it. So, it is not a recent discovery,” Akan said.
He reiterated the community’s claim that the surrounding area belonged to Ebute-Igbooro, adding that the spring had historically been used by their forefathers.
“The fathers before us who gave birth to my own parents were already worshipping it here in Ebute,” he said.
Akan also spoke about the growing interest in the water, claiming that visitors from different parts of Nigeria and abroad had been coming to the location to collect it for prayers and traditional purposes.
“As it is right now, people come all the way from abroad, from Abuja, and from everywhere to fetch this water,” he said.
He appealed to the Ogun State Government to intervene by providing infrastructure and helping the community transform the location into a modern cultural and tourism destination.
“We want the government to assist us with it—to help elevate our Yoruba cultural heritage, to modernise it, and to turn it into something great and remarkable,” Akan said.
He specifically called for improved access roads, fencing, renovation and other basic facilities that could make the site suitable for visitors.

title: “It’s Not the Whole Story”: Aral School Participants Rethink Karakalpakstan
content:
A proverb about seasonal food caught the attention of Australian researcher, multimedia artist, and producer Jess Nikitina-Li while she was at the Aral School in Nukus.
“I’m interested in language, art and storytelling, and I didn’t really know what I would be working on during the program, but I became obsessed with this proverbial wisdom that kept coming up when we started asking questions about food systems in Karakalpakstan,” she told The Times of Central Asia. One proverb in particular became important to her work: “Three months of pumpkin, three months fish, three months melon, three months milk. All four seasons of the year the people are well fed and a lot of sweet fruit we have in our lands.”
“This really grounded my thinking because it reflects my belief that people are not inherently depleted,” she said. “People become depleted through extraction. Seasonal abundance has always been in this land, and people know how to work with the seasons; people are adaptive.”
The school is an initiative of the Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation (ACDF). Its first cohort studied food and water at a household level. Applications for the second cohort, which will explore the theme of “Climate and Landscape” from January to June 2027, are open until October 25.
TCA spoke with participants about their work in Karakalpakstan.
Nikitina-Li became particularly interested in the role of women within households, including kelin, a term referring to a young bride or daughter-in-law. “One of the key projects I worked on was a project called Tabak,” she said. “Tabak is a specifically resonant symbol in Karakalpakstan. It is the iron plate that everyone traditionally eats from.”
Her work with women eventually led to the creation of a cooking collective called “The Wild Kelin,” through which participants explored traditional recipes, nutrition, seasonality, and the knowledge passed between generations.
“I wanted to see what was important to them, what was relevant to their households, because that to me is the test of what is relevant to this region,” she said.
“We did a lot of community programming, textbook research, field research, field recordings and filmmaking, but the most important thing for me was done in close collaboration with our local colleagues,” she told TCA. “This was really a priority for me. It was why I came here, to have this strong intercultural exchange and to make solidarities with the land and with the people who understand the land the best.”
“We didn’t do this through this lens of people as victims, but through a lens of empowerment and understanding people as having agency – that they have an inherent capability of keeping themselves, and each other, alive,” Nikitina-Li said. “Something unique to this program was understanding how to create a community – a community of thinkers and makers who are grounded in the same principles, values and ethos, but who work so differently.”
“My biggest takeaway from the first cohort is wow – this was very well curated in terms of people. You have engineers and ecologists, and you have chefs, and then someone like me in art and anthropology. It encourages these different fields, but also the in-betweens, to really come through and collectivize. We all work so differently, but essentially we worked from the same starting point of caring for this place and understanding that people here already know so much.”
“There is conflict that happens, but this was an important part of community building. This is something I will take away with me, the understanding that through tension and difficulty a community can be built. I learnt so much about cultural resilience that wouldn’t have been possible sitting behind a computer or being at home.”
“I’ve learnt so much from being able to visit people’s families,” she said. “I’ve learnt about how a household functions, how a neighborhood functions, how a community functions, how people sustain each other through generations. This region can be painted through a lens of disaster and collapse and crisis, but people here are so joyous. This is what I mean when I talk about learning about what cultural and community resilience means.”
Bekmurat Abdikairov, a researcher from Karakalpakstan, specializes in geographic information systems (GIS) and remote sensing. His research uses geospatial analysis to examine changes in agricultural land, with Chimbay district serving as a case study.
“Participating in the Aral School was a very valuable experience for me, both professionally and personally,” he said. “As a young researcher from Karakalpakstan working on environmental issues, I had the opportunity to meet researchers, experts, and young professionals from different countries and to exchange perspectives on the challenges facing the Aral region.”
“One of the main things I gained was a broader understanding of the Aral crisis,” he told TCA. “Before the School, I was mostly looking at the region through the perspective of scientific research, particularly soil salinity, land degradation, remote sensing, and GIS. The School helped me see that these environmental problems cannot be considered separately from water management, agriculture, climate change, public health, livelihoods, and the social dimensions of the region.”
“What particularly impressed me was the diversity of perspectives,” Abdikairov said. “People from different disciplines and countries may look at the same problem differently, and bringing these perspectives together can lead to new ideas and more comprehensive solutions.”
Abdikairov’s work draws on satellite imagery and machine-learning approaches to monitor soil salinity and land conditions.
“The School reminded me that technological approaches should be connected with field observations and local knowledge,” he said. “Satellite data can show where changes are occurring, but understanding why those changes are happening requires cooperation between scientists, local communities, institutions, and policymakers.”
Islam Nurmukhamedov, a geophysicist born in Nukus and educated in Tashkent, is a PhD researcher focusing on ecology at the Karakalpak Scientific Research Institute of Natural Sciences.
“As a geophysicist and ecology researcher in Karakalpakstan, I believe that groundwater is still poorly studied, particularly its levels, composition, and available volume,” he told TCA. “This issue is becoming even more important as global warming and climate change continue to affect the region.”
“First, there is a language barrier and cultural differences between local communities and the international community. Another important issue is the low level of trust that local communities sometimes have toward external organizations and researchers. Aral School provides a valuable platform for breaking down these barriers and building cooperation between local and international communities,” Nurmukhamedov said. “It creates an opportunity to exchange knowledge, understand different perspectives, and develop projects together.”
A discussion with an international participant turned to construction. “I realized that local materials can be very well adapted to our dry and harsh climate,” he said. “They can also be more environmentally friendly and affordable. I think combining local knowledge with modern scientific approaches can lead to more sustainable solutions for our region.”
Sarthak Chakraborty, an interactive media artist and photogrammetrist based in India, works with indigenous knowledge systems and 3D technologies.
“I had a perspective and a knowledge of this place before coming,” he said. “I had consumed all the media through the internet, and I was told a story of scarcity, and that is what was fed. What I discovered when I came was very different. I expected it to be worse here based on the narrative I got online. But then after coming here, I feel like it’s a story of scarcity that has been sold, and that should not be the case. There’s so much life, there’s so much energy; there is so much wildlife: the plants, the animals, the people.”
“I found this book in the Aral School library called Deserts are Not Empty that talks about living as a state of mind,” he told TCA. “There are so many microorganisms; there are so many fungi. There are people still living in that space; they’re also embodying the region. They’re surviving. And when you visit Moynaq, you feel that scarcity, the emptiness; you feel like time has stopped in that place, but it’s not the whole story.”

title: Italian-Australian icon Franco Cozzo remembered in retail revival
content:
Italian-Australian icon Franco Cozzo fondly recalled in retail revival
With his animated appearance and distinctive dialect, Franco Cozzo inadvertently became a Melbourne cultural icon while flogging furniture on commercial television.
Best known for his 'Megalo!' catchphrase and pronouncing the inner-west suburb of Footscray as 'Foot-iz-kraay', the ebullient businessman was one of the first emphatically Italian-Australian voices on the small screen at a time when many first-generation European migrants flattened their accents.
Cozzo opened his first furniture showroom in North Melbourne in 1959, after years wearing out his shoe leather as a door-to-door electrical appliance salesman.
Less than a decade later, he expanded his enterprise to establish his best-known outlet — a three-storey edifice in Footscray, which closed in 2018 and is now a craft brewery.
The Franco Cozzo name is also emblazoned on a Sydney Road shopfront in Brunswick, which reopened over the weekend, three years on from the death of its founder, aged 88.
Filmmaker Madeleine Martiniello documented the furniture retailer's career in the 2021 feature Palazzo di Cozzo and said his profile transcended business to become a cultural institution.
The film shows Cozzo's cameo appearances on The Don Lane Show, a Franco parody on 1990s ABC youth program Recovery and even more recent sampling in electronic dance music.
"I think Franco Cozzo presented to Melbourne an example what a migrant can achieve when they come to this country,"Martiniello said.
"I don't just mean that in an entrepreneurial sense, but I mean it in a cultural sense as well.
"I like to think of Franco as someone who built a wonderful life for himself but also managed to become part of the cultural fabric of the city.
"The fact that people are still interested in his shop and the next generation taking over shows that he really meant something on a hyper-local scale to Melburnians."
Several of Cozzo's children have revived his eponymous Brunswick store after a five-year hiatus, with a grand reopening over the weekend.
The Sicilian bonhomie was as conspicuous as the complimentary cannoli and a Italian tricolour archway welcoming customers old and new.
Daughter Alessia Cozzo said the retail revival was inspired by her father's lamentations in his latter years that the next generation would not follow in his footsteps.
"It was at the dinner table, chatting about the shops and … [Dad] said: 'I don't think you guys are going to continue'," she said.
"And we were all said: 'No Papa, we're going to bring back the shop and the sales through generations and generations.' That's how we made the promise to him.
"Papa passing away didn't make it easy but we want to carry on his legacy."
At the weekend reopening, Alessia said her late father's larger-than-life persona was a hard act to follow.
She said despite the showroom hiatus, demand for the distinctive Sicilian baroque-style furniture remained strong in the 2020s.
"He'd be so excited. He'd be so happy and so proud of his four daughters and that he had grown such strong Italian women," she said.
"It's been a long process [to reopen the Brunswick store]. There's a room at the front that's dedicated to Dad. It's got all of his beautiful furniture there and we have a whole wall as a tribute."
Madeleine Martiniello noted that Australian commercial television of the 1980s was highly Anglocentric, with the 1980 debut of SBS TV providing the main multicultural platform on the small screen.
"Franco is a very special character in Melbourne's cultural identity,"the filmmaker said.
"He presented this successful migrant figure but there was also something about his character that was loveable and enticing.
"When I was making the documentary, people would always ask me: 'Is anyone even buying that furniture?' It was something I wanted to answer.
"There's quite an eclectic mix of people that are interested in the Cozzo baroque style: from the classic older Italian migrants to people who have this post-modern appreciation of it.
"I think people may be asking the same question of the reopening of the shop: 'Is anyone going to buying this furniture; is this business going to be viable?'
"I'm really happy to see his daughters do feel there is a future. I'm interested to see how the cultural meaning of the furniture and the store as landmark evolves."

title: How Iraq’s iconic masgouf fish found a home in Dubai
content: Dubai: Unlike most grilled fish dishes, Iraqi masgouf is not cooked directly over a flame. Instead, the fish is opened, cleaned and seasoned before being placed beside glowing embers, where it cooks slowly under the careful supervision of the chef.The process is as important as the dish itself. Time, patience and constant attention to the fire are central to a tradition that has been passed down through generations of Iraqi families and has travelled far beyond the banks of the Tigris and Euphrates.In Dubai, masgouf has found a new audience among Emiratis and residents from a wide range of nationalities, evolving from a dish associated primarily with the Iraqi community into one of the emirate's recognised culinary experiences.Decades of traditionChef Azad MohammedFor Chef Azad Mohammed's family, the story of masgouf dates back to 1973 in Iraqi Kurdistan, where the family first began preparing the dish.In 1999, they brought that experience to the UAE through Erbil Iraqi Kebab restaurant, carrying with them skills and techniques accumulated over decades. The profession remained within the family, with knowledge passed down from one generation to the next, making the preparation of masgouf both a craft and a family tradition.Traditionally, masgouf is associated with river fish and open-fire cooking, making it an integral part of Iraqi food culture. Yet its significance extends beyond its ingredients. Preparation requires space, time and careful management of the fire, creating a visual spectacle for diners waiting for their meal.The fish is opened and placed near the embers, allowing heat to reach it gradually. The chef continuously monitors the fire, adjusting temperature, distance and cooking time to achieve the desired result.Azad said handling the fire, selecting the right fish and preparing it correctly are inseparable from the quality of masgouf, adding that years of experience have helped his family preserve the traditional method they learned in Iraq.A craft learned through experienceMuch of the knowledge involved in preparing masgouf remains unwritten.Like many traditional dishes, masgouf carries more than flavour. Picture: Dennis MallariChefs learn to read the heat of the fire, judge when the fish should be moved closer or further away and monitor subtle changes during the grilling process. Over time, these skills become practical knowledge transmitted through generations.According to Azad, mastering these details requires years of experience.He noted that not every type of fish is suitable for preparing masgouf in the traditional Iraqi style, as different varieties vary in texture and their ability to withstand the slow grilling method.Among the fish commonly used are sea bream and sea bass, with understanding their characteristics forming an essential part of the chef's expertise.More than a mealLike many traditional dishes, masgouf carries more than flavour.The aroma of the wood fire, the anticipation surrounding the cooking process and the gathering of family and friends around the fish become part of the experience and memory associated with the dish.When masgouf travels to a new city, it carries not only a recipe but also the customs and stories connected to it. The dining table becomes a space where a piece of its place of origin is recreated.Restaurant owners say the dish's popularity in Dubai extends well beyond Iraqi diners and increasingly includes Emiratis and residents from different cultural backgrounds.Its growing presence reflects the broader exchange of culinary traditions within Dubai's multicultural society, where food often serves as an introduction to another culture.Numbers behind the traditionAccording to Azad, between 100 and 150 fish are prepared daily, with each fish averaging around four kilograms in weight.This amounts to between 400 and 600 kilograms of fish being prepared every day.The figures highlight the scale of the operation and the labour-intensive nature of the craft. Each fish must be cleaned, prepared and carefully grilled, with the process relying on experience and constant supervision of the fire.In an era when many kitchens prioritise speed, masgouf remains deliberately slow. The fish needs time, the fire demands attention and customers must wait.For many diners, however, that waiting is part of the experience.One restaurant customer summed up the connection simply by saying: "I never miss Friday."For many families, the dish has become part of a weekly ritual centred on gathering together.A journey that continuesIn Dubai, where cuisines and cultures from around the world meet, masgouf has found a new audience without abandoning the elements that define it: fish, fire, time and expertise.Between the glowing embers and the dining table, the dish continues its journey as more than just a meal. It remains a craft that carries the memory of a place, a cooking tradition passed down through generations and a culinary experience that has crossed borders while retaining its Iraqi identity.

title: India’s shapeshifting chutneys: Memories on a plate
content:
It’s a dash of flavour that defies definition, changing from one community to another, from one region to another. It’s a shapeshifter that can be dry, coarse, runny or thick. “Our culinary landscape is vast and incredibly nuanced, and the concept of chutney is also limitless,” says award-winning author and culinary chronicler Rushina Munshaw-Ghildiyal, who spent nearly a decade documenting chutneys across the country. In 2017, she also started Indian Food Observance Days and one of the ten days was dedicated to chutneys. It was celebrated year on year. She put out an open call for people across the country to celebrate it in any way they liked. It picked up, with people using #ChutneyDay to share stories and recipes. Brands joined in, and September 24 is now celebrated as Chutney Day.
Last year, it all came together in the form of a deliciously illustrated, over-500-page book, Chutney: A Compendium of Stories and Recipes. It features around 230 recipes and inputs from over 120 regional food experts, capturing what chutneys look like across India — from Kashmir, Haryana, Jharkhand, Manipur, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh to communities such as the Bohri, Sindhi, Saraswat, Anglo-Indian and Syrian Christian.




For Munshaw-Ghildiyal, the reasons for embarking on this journey were two-fold: chutney connects people on a fundamental level and it has also suffered from homogenisation.
“Similar to how people talk about ‘curry’ not really existing as a single dish, chutney too underwent a broad-stroke flattening as it travelled around the world,” she says. “Even the word ‘chutney’ was popularised by the colonials; different parts of India historically had different names for it. In the south, it was recorded as thuvaiyal. Ayurvedic texts refer to it as katni or catni, and lehya — inspired by the act of licking. Traditionally, it was just a small dot on the plate.”
Using whatever is on hand
Food chronicler Kashmiri Nath recalls Kharoli, a pungent fermented mustard condiment commonly eaten with food in Assam during summers. Semi-fine pounded mustard is mixed with lime juice and a little khar, wrapped in banana leaves and left to ferment in an earthen jar for five to six days.
For Kashmiri Nath, 56, an Assamese food chronicler, chutney was “something fun — created out of nothing.” A little leftover fresh green pea curry, for instance, could become one. The same resourcefulness shaped Anuradha Joshi Medhora’s childhood in Indore. There was a chutney with every meal and it was, as she puts it, “the flavour bomb”. What went into it depended on what came from the family garden: amrud, amla, dhania, pudina, kairi, narangi, shehtut, figs, mahua. Then there were the scraps — lauki, pumpkin, ridge gourd and ivy gourd peels, toasted with sesame, mustard, lime and whatever else was at hand. Then, of course, the beej ki chutneys: kathal ke beej, kaddu ke beej, tarbooz ke beej, lauki ke beej. Whatever seeds you had, you found a way to turn them into something delicious.”
